words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.ex: The loud noise exasperates me.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让我感到烦躁。
words.en: If someone or something exasperates you, they annoy you and make you feel frustrated or impatient.

words.tr: adj. 狂怒的；暴怒的；激烈的
words.ex: He was furious when he lost his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了钥匙时非常生气。
words.en: If someone is furious, they are extremely angry.

words.ex: He shouted with fury when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他输掉比赛时，他愤怒地大喊。
words.en: Fury is a feeling of intense anger.

words.tr: adj. 爱发牢骚的；脾气坏的；不悦的； 愠怒的
words.ex: He is grouchy when he wakes up early.
words.ex_cn: 他早起时脾气很暴躁。
words.en: If someone is grouchy, they are bad-tempered and complain a lot.

words.tr:
n. 熏香；熏香的烟
v. 使愤怒；激怒
words.ex: The smell of incense fills the room.
words.ex_cn: 香火的气味充满了房间。
words.en: Incense is a substance that is burned for its pleasant smell, often used in religious ceremonies. As a verb, to incense means to make someone very angry.

words.ex: He felt indignant when they blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他们把错误归咎于他时，他感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you are indignant, you are shocked and angry, because you think that something is unjust or unfair.

words.ex: The unfair verdict caused public outrage.
words.ex_cn: 不公正的判决引发了公众的愤怒。
words.en: An outrage is an extremely strong reaction of anger, shock, or indignation.

words.tr: adj. 热情的；充满热情的；
words.ex: She is passionate about teaching children.
words.ex_cn: 她对教孩子充满热情。
words.en: Having, showing, or caused by strong feelings or beliefs.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.ex: He burst into rage when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他勃然大怒。
words.en: Rage is a feeling of intense anger that is difficult to control.

words.ex: He felt indignation when he saw the unfair rule.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到不公平的规则时，他感到愤怒。
words.en: Indignation is a feeling of anger and surprise which you have when you think that something is wrong or unfair.

words.ex: He gave a vehement reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了激烈的回答。
words.en: If a person or their actions or comments are vehement, the person has very strong feelings or opinions and expresses them forcefully.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 感觉

words.tr: adj. 狂怒的；暴怒的；激烈的
words.ex: He was furious when he lost his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了钥匙时非常生气。
words.en: If someone is furious, they are extremely angry.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 好奇

words.tr: adj. 狂怒的；暴怒的；激烈的
words.ex: He was furious when he lost his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了钥匙时非常生气。
words.en: If someone is furious, they are extremely angry.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 焦急

words.tr: adj. 狂怒的；暴怒的；激烈的
words.ex: He was furious when he lost his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了钥匙时非常生气。
words.en: If someone is furious, they are extremely angry.

words.tr:
v. 使烦恼；使不安
n. 不安；忧虑；烦恼
words.ex: The loud noise disquieted her.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让她感到烦恼。
words.en: Disquiet is a feeling of worry or anxiety.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 惊讶

words.tr: v. 使惊讶；“astonish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was astonished by the sudden news.
words.ex_cn: 他被这个突然的消息惊呆了。
words.en: If you are astonished by something, you are very surprised about it.

words.ex: The magic trick will astonish you.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术会让你惊讶。
words.en: If something or someone astonishes you, they surprise you very much.

words.ex: The magic trick astounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们惊呆了。
words.en: If something astounds you, it surprises or shocks you very much.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is breathtaking.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色令人惊叹。
words.en: If you say that something is breathtaking, you mean that it is extremely beautiful or amazing.

words.ex: He felt dismay when he saw the low grade.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到低分时，感到沮丧。
words.en: Dismay is a feeling of unhappiness and disappointment.

words.ex: It is inconceivable that he forgot his own birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他忘了自己生日，这简直难以想象。
words.en: If something is inconceivable, it is impossible to imagine or believe because it is so unlikely.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is marvelous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色极好。
words.en: If you describe something as marvelous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely good.

words.tr: v. 使石化；使僵化；吓呆
words.ex: The lightning petrified the tree into stone.
words.ex_cn: 闪电把树变成了石头。
words.en: To petrify means to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think.

words.ex: The loud noise scared the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子。
words.en: If something scares you, it frightens or worries you.

words.ex: The loud noise startle the bird.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音惊动了那只鸟。
words.en: If something or someone startles you, they surprise and frighten you slightly.

words.tr: adj. 引人注目的；显著的； v. 打击；“strike”的现在分词；
words.ex: The painting has a striking color scheme.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有着引人注目的配色。
words.en: Something that is striking is very noticeable or unusual.

words.ex: The loud noise stunned him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他震惊了。
words.en: To stun someone means to shock or surprise them very much.

words.tr: v. 使说不出话来；使目瞪口呆
words.ex: The magic trick dumbfound everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让所有人都惊呆了。
words.en: If someone or something dumbfounds you, they surprise you so much that you cannot think or speak for a moment.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.ex: The concert was fabulous!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something as fabulous, you are emphasizing that you like it a lot or think that it is very good.

words.ex: The sunset was spectacular.
words.ex_cn: 日落非常壮观。
words.en: Something that is spectacular is very impressive or dramatic.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 沮丧

words.tr: adj. 不快乐的；忧郁的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room was cheerless and dark.
words.ex_cn: 房间阴暗而无生气。
words.en: If you describe a place or a thing as cheerless, you mean that it is dull and depressing.

words.ex: The rain dampened the sound of the drums.
words.ex_cn: 雨减弱了鼓声。
words.en: To dampen something means to make it slightly wet, or to make it less strong or intense.

words.tr:
adj. 沮丧的；低落的；垂头丧气的
v. 使…情绪低落；使沮丧；“deject”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt dejected after failing the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格后感到沮丧。
words.en: If you are dejected, you feel miserable or unhappy, especially because you have just been disappointed by something.

words.tr: v. 压下；降低；使沮丧；使不活泼；使萧条
words.ex: He depresses the button to start the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他按下按钮启动机器。
words.en: If something depresses you, it makes you feel sad and disappointed.

words.ex: He felt deep depression after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的抑郁。
words.en: A period during which business, employment, and stock-market values decline severely or remain at a very low level of activity.

words.ex: The sky was dismal and gray all day.
words.ex_cn: 天空一整天都是阴沉灰暗的。
words.en: If you describe something as dismal, you mean that it is very bad or depressing.

words.ex: The downcast eyes of the boy showed he was sad.
words.ex_cn: 男孩低垂的眼睛显示出他很难过。
words.en: If you are downcast, you are feeling sad and without hope.

words.tr: adj. 无精打采的；疲倦无力的
words.ex: He gave a languid smile before lying down.
words.ex_cn: 他躺下前给了一个慵懒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as languid, you mean that they show little energy or interest and are very slow and casual in their movements.

words.tr:
adj. 俯卧的；平卧的；给（悲伤等）压倒的
v. 使俯伏；使拜倒
words.ex: He fell prostrate on the ground after the race.
words.ex_cn: 比赛后，他瘫倒在了地上。
words.en: If you prostrate yourself, you lie down flat on the ground, usually in front of someone, as a way of showing respect or submission. It can also mean to be extremely tired or emotionally drained.

words.tr: adj. 黑暗的；幽暗的；忧郁的；沮丧的
words.ex: The room was gloomy with no windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间没有窗户，很黑暗。
words.en: If a place is gloomy, it is almost dark so that you cannot see very well. If people are gloomy, they are unhappy and have no hope.

words.tr: adj.  忧郁的；阴沉的；阴暗的
words.ex: The room had a somber mood.
words.ex_cn: 房间里有一种阴郁的气氛。
words.en: If someone is somber, they are serious or sad.

words.ex: The bad news dispirited the whole team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息让整个团队士气低落。
words.en: If something dispirits you, it makes you lose your enthusiasm and excitement.

words.tr: v. 使士气低落；使失去斗志
words.ex: The bad news demoralized the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队士气低落。
words.en: If something demoralizes someone, it makes them lose so much confidence in what they are doing that they want to give up.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 恐惧

words.ex: The dog cowers when the thunder sounds.
words.ex_cn: 当雷声响起时，狗会蜷缩起来。
words.en: To crouch down in fear.

words.tr:
v. 害怕；畏惧
n. 恐惧；畏惧
words.ex: He dreads going to the dentist.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕去看牙医。
words.en: If you dread something, you fear it intensely.

words.ex: The storm was formidable and destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴很可怕，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as formidable, you mean that you feel slightly frightened by them because they are very great or impressive.

words.ex: The loud noise gave her a sudden fright.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让她吓了一跳。
words.en: A sudden intense feeling of fear.

words.ex: The horror of the dark made her scream.
words.ex_cn: 对黑暗的恐惧让她尖叫。
words.en: A feeling of great fear, shock, or disgust.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.tr:
n. 恐慌；
v. 感到恐慌；
words.ex: A panic spread through the crowd when the fire alarm rang.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了恐慌。
words.en: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

words.ex: The loud thunder terrified the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的雷声吓坏了那个孩子。
words.en: If something terrifies you, it makes you feel extremely frightened.

words.ex: The movie caused a feeling of terror in the audience.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影让观众感到恐怖。
words.en: Terror is a very strong feeling of fear, especially fear that you experience suddenly.

words.ex: He loves to dance to funk music on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在周末随着放克音乐跳舞。
words.en: Funk can refer to a state of fear or depression, or to a style of music that combines elements of rhythm and blues, soul, and jazz.

words.ex: He felt trepidation before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到恐惧。
words.en: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

words.ex: He is xenophobic and dislikes foreigners.
words.ex_cn: 他有排外心理，不喜欢外国人。
words.en: If you describe someone as xenophobic, you disapprove of them because they show strong dislike or fear of people from other countries.

words.tr: v. 恐吓；恫吓；实施恐怖统治
words.ex: The bully tries to terrorize the new student.
words.ex_cn: 这个霸凌者试图恐吓新学生。
words.en: To terrorize someone means to make them very frightened by using violence or threats.

words.ex: He threatened to call the police.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁要叫警察。
words.en: If someone threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 狂热

words.ex: He wore a crazy hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶疯狂的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as crazy, you mean that they are very enthusiastic or excited about something.

words.tr:
adj. 狂热入迷的；盲信的
n. 狂热者；盲信者
words.ex: He is a fanatic fan of soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他对足球狂热入迷。
words.en: A fanatic is a person who is very enthusiastic about and devoted to a particular activity, cause, or belief, often to an extreme degree.

words.ex: His fanaticism for the team made him miss work.
words.ex_cn: 他对球队的狂热让他错过了工作。
words.en: Fanaticism is the quality of being fanatical, which means having very extreme and often unreasonable beliefs, especially in politics or religion.

words.tr:
n. 狂乱；狂暴；狂怒
v. 使狂乱；使狂怒
words.ex: The crowd went into a frenzy when the singer appeared.
words.ex_cn: 当歌手出现时，人群陷入了狂热。
words.en: A frenzy is a state of uncontrolled excitement or wild behavior.

words.tr: adj. 疯狂的；精神失常的；精神错乱的
words.ex: He thinks it's insane to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 他认为无证驾驶是疯狂的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as insane, you mean that they are very foolish or crazy.

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: The new song caused a furor among teenagers.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌在青少年中引起了狂热。
words.en: A furor is a very angry or excited reaction by people to something.

words.ex: The children were running in a frenetic way around the room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房间里发狂似的跑来跑去。
words.en: If you describe an activity as frenetic, you mean that it is fast and energetic, but rather uncontrolled and often not very well organized.

words.ex: His political speeches were often filled with zealotry and fanaticism.
words.ex_cn: 他的政治演讲常常充满了狂热和偏执。
words.en: Zealotry is excessive or fanatical devotion to a cause, often to the point of being blind to its faults.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 满意

words.tr:
n. 内容；含量；
adj. 满足的；
words.ex: The content of the video is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这个视频的内容非常有趣。
words.en: Content refers to the things that are held or included in something, or the state of being happy and satisfied.

words.ex: He gratifies his parents by getting good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他通过取得好成绩来让父母感到欣慰。
words.en: If you are gratified by something, it gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.tr: adj. 感到宽慰的； v. 缓解；“relieve”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt relieved when he passed the exam.
words.ex_cn: 当他通过考试时，他感到宽慰。
words.en: If you are relieved, you feel happy because something unpleasant has not happened or is no longer happening.

words.tr: v. 使饱足；使厌腻；充分满足
words.ex: The big meal satiated his hunger.
words.ex_cn: 这顿丰盛的饭填饱了他的肚子。
words.en: To satisfy a desire or need fully.

words.ex: The teacher gave a satisfactory grade.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个令人满意的分数。
words.en: If something is satisfactory, it is good enough or acceptable.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 梦想

words.ex: His aspiration is to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他的渴望是成为一名医生。
words.en: A strong desire to achieve something high or great.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.ex: The case will be heard in court next week.
words.ex_cn: 这个案件将于下周在法院审理。
words.en: A court is a place where legal matters are decided by a judge and jury or by a magistrate.

words.ex: He craves chocolate when he is stressed.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到压力时，他渴望吃巧克力。
words.en: If you crave something, or crave for it, you want to have it very much.

words.tr: adj. 值得拥有的；令人渴望的；称心如意的；
words.ex: A quiet neighborhood is desirable for families.
words.ex_cn: 安静的社区对家庭来说是值得拥有的。
words.en: Something that is desirable is worth having or doing because it is useful, necessary, or popular.

words.tr:
n. 欲望；渴望；
v. 渴望；期望；
words.ex: He felt a strong desire to travel the world.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种强烈的环游世界的欲望。
words.en: A strong feeling of wanting to have something or wishing for something to happen.

words.ex: He is desirous of a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他想要一辆新自行车。
words.en: Having or characterized by desire; wanting or wishing for something.

words.ex: He felt hunger after running for an hour.
words.ex_cn: 他跑了一个小时后感到饥饿。
words.en: A strong desire or need for food.

words.tr:
adj. 长时间的；长的；
adv. 始终；长久地；
n. 长期；长时间；
v. 盼望；渴望；
words.ex: We had a long meeting yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨天开了一个长时间的会议。
words.en: Having a great distance from one end to the other; extending over a large area.

words.tr: adj. 关怀的；切望的；惦记的；悬虑的
words.ex: He was solicitous about her health.
words.ex_cn: 他非常关心她的健康。
words.en: If you are solicitous, you are very concerned about someone's safety, health, or comfort.

words.ex: His ambition is to become a president.
words.ex_cn: 他的野心是成为总统。
words.en: An ambition is a strong desire to achieve something, typically requiring determination and hard work.

words.ex: He sat by the window in reverie.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边，沉浸在遐想中。
words.en: A reverie is a state of imagining or thinking about pleasant things, often as a way of escaping from reality.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 情感

words.ex: She showed great affection for her little dog.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的小狗非常钟爱。
words.en: A feeling of liking and caring for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 挚爱的；有深厚感情的；充满深情的
words.ex: She is affectionate with her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她对弟弟很亲昵。
words.en: If you are affectionate, you show your love or fondness for another person in the way that you behave towards them.

words.tr: v. 珍爱；爱惜；怀念；怀有（感情）；抱有（希望）
words.ex: I cherish the time I spend with my family.
words.ex_cn: 我珍惜与家人共度的时光。
words.en: If you cherish something, you care for it lovingly and protect it carefully.

words.ex: He gave an emotional speech about his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于他母亲的感人演讲。
words.en: Something that is emotional is connected with people's feelings. If someone is emotional, they show their feelings very openly, especially because they are upset.

words.tr: adj. 使感动的；感情的；动感情的
words.ex: The movie used emotive music to make people cry.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影用了富有情感的音乐来让人流泪。
words.en: If you describe something as emotive, you mean that it is concerned with emotions and feelings, and often causes them.

words.ex: He remained impassive when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个坏消息时，他依然面无表情。
words.en: If someone is impassive, they do not show any emotion.

words.tr: adj. 失恋的；害相思病的
words.ex: He felt lovelorn after she left him.
words.ex_cn: 她离开他后，他感到失恋痛苦。
words.en: Someone who is lovelorn is unhappy because they are in love with someone who does not love them.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 热情

words.tr: adj. 热情的；充满热情的；
words.ex: She is passionate about teaching children.
words.ex_cn: 她对教孩子充满热情。
words.en: Having, showing, or caused by strong feelings or beliefs.

words.tr: adj. 感伤的；感情的；多愁善感的
words.ex: He kept the old toy because he was sentimental about it.
words.ex_cn: 他保留了那个旧玩具，因为他对它有感情。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sentimental, you mean that they are influenced by emotional feelings, especially about happy memories of past events or relationships with other people, rather than by careful thought and judgment based on facts.

words.tr: v. 触摸；接触；“touch”的现在分词；
words.ex: The child is touching the soft blanket.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在触摸柔软的毯子。
words.en: If something is touching, it causes feelings of sadness or sympathy.

words.ex: He showed apathy toward the news.
words.ex_cn: 他对这则新闻漠不关心。
words.en: Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, or concern about something. It is a state of indifference, or the suppression of emotions such as concern, excitement, motivation, or passion.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.tr: adj. 充满热情的；热心的；
words.ex: He is enthusiastic about playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他对打篮球充满热情。
words.en: If you are enthusiastic about something, you show how much you like or enjoy it by the way that you behave and talk.

words.ex: He showed great zeal in helping others.
words.ex_cn: 他在帮助他人时表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Zeal is great enthusiasm, especially in connection with work, religion, or politics.

words.ex: He is zealous about helping others.
words.ex_cn: 他热心帮助别人。
words.en: If someone is zealous, they are enthusiastic and eager about something, especially something they believe in very strongly.

words.tr: n. 兴致；热情；趣味；（用于调味的）柠檬皮；橙皮
words.ex: He cooks with zest and loves spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他做菜很有激情，喜欢辣的食物。
words.en: Great enthusiasm and energy.

words.ex: He is an ardent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: An ardent person has strong feelings or enthusiasm for something.

words.ex: He speaks with great ardor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Ardor is a strong, intense feeling of love or enthusiasm for someone or something.

words.tr: v. 投入；献身；“devote”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 全心全意的；投入的；
words.ex: He devoted all his time to helping his students.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有时间都投入到了帮助学生上。
words.en: If you are devoted to something, you care about it a lot and are very enthusiastic about it.

words.ex: He showed great enthusiasm for learning English.
words.ex_cn: 他对学习英语表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Enthusiasm is a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something and a desire to become involved in it.

words.tr:
n. 冰雹；
v. 把…誉为；
words.ex: The hail broke many car windows.
words.ex_cn: 冰雹打碎了许多汽车窗户。
words.en: Hail is small balls of ice that fall like rain from the sky. It can also mean to call out to someone in order to attract their attention, or to praise someone enthusiastically.

words.ex: The climate is hospitable for growing oranges.
words.ex_cn: 这种气候适合种植橙子。
words.en: If someone is hospitable, they are friendly, welcoming, and generous to guests or strangers.

words.tr:
adj. 慷慨激昂的；热烈的
v. 激起热情；使激动；“impassion”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He gave an impassioned speech about peace.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了充满激情的关于和平的演讲。
words.en: An impassioned speech or piece of writing is one that expresses very strong feelings about something.

words.ex: He spoke with fervor about his dreams.
words.ex_cn: 他充满热情地谈论自己的梦想。
words.en: Fervor is intense and passionate feeling.

words.tr: adj. 热烈的；强烈的；热情的
words.ex: He is a fervent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: having or showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

words.ex: His dedication to teaching helped many students succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他对教学的奉献帮助了许多学生取得成功。
words.en: The act of dedicating or the state of being dedicated; commitment.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 态度

words.tr: v. 嫉妒；羡慕；不乐意地做（或付出）
words.ex: He begrudges his friend's success.
words.ex_cn: 他嫉妒朋友的成功。
words.en: If you begrudge something, you feel unhappy or resentful about having to give it, do it, or allow it.

words.tr: adj. 深感懊悔的；痛悔的；悔悟的
words.ex: He felt contrite after lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他在对母亲撒谎后感到悔恨。
words.en: Feeling or expressing remorse or penitence; affected by guilt.

words.tr: adj. 不顾一切的；极度渴望的；绝望的；
words.ex: He made a desperate attempt to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾一切地试图救那个孩子。
words.en: If you are desperate, you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to try anything to change it.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；讨好
adj. 更平坦的；更扁平的；“flat”的比较级
adv. 更平直地；更直截了当地；“flat”的比较级
words.ex: He flatters his boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that may be sincere or may be intended to persuade you to do something.

words.tr: adj. 绝望的；孤立无助的；被弃置的
words.ex: The forlorn dog sat by the door, waiting for its owner.
words.ex_cn: 那条孤单的狗坐在门边，等待它的主人。
words.en: If someone is forlorn, they feel alone and unhappy.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.ex: He is jealous of his brother's new bike.
words.ex_cn: 他嫉妒他弟弟的新自行车。
words.en: If someone is jealous, they feel angry or bitter because they think that another person is trying to take a lover or friend, or a possession, away from them.

words.tr:
adj. 亵渎的；不敬神的；世俗的
v. 亵渎神灵；亵圣
words.ex: He used profane words during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵中说了脏话。
words.en: If someone uses profane language, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, especially because it refers to sex or other bodily functions in a way that is considered inappropriate.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 犹豫

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.tr:
n. 顾虑；顾忌；踌躇
v. 顾虑；有顾忌
words.ex: He had a scruple about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对于对朋友撒谎感到不安。
words.en: A scruple is a feeling of doubt or hesitation with regard to the morality or propriety of a course of action.

words.tr:
v. 挣扎；深陷困境
n. 比目鱼
words.ex: The fish floundered in the shallow water.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在浅水中挣扎。
words.en: If you flounder, you experience great difficulties and are likely to fail completely.

words.ex: He hesitates to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他犹豫着是否要寻求帮助。
words.en: If you hesitate, you pause slightly while you are doing something or just before you do it, usually because you are uncertain, embarrassed, or worried.

words.tr: n. 优柔寡断；犹豫不决
words.ex: He showed indecision when choosing between the two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择两份工作时表现出犹豫不决。
words.en: Indecision is the inability to make decisions quickly and effectively.

words.tr: v. 游移不定；踌躇；犹豫
words.ex: He vacillates between choosing tea or coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择茶还是咖啡之间犹豫不决。
words.en: To vacillate means to waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.

words.ex: He wavers when choosing between two jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他在两个工作之间摇摆不定。
words.en: If you waver, you cannot decide about something or you are uncertain about what you should do.

words.tr: adj. 无决断的；犹豫不决的
words.ex: He was irresolute about which job to accept.
words.ex_cn: 他对于接受哪份工作犹豫不决。
words.en: If someone is irresolute, they are uncertain about what to do or are unable to make decisions.

words.tr:
adj. 蹒跚的；不稳的；支吾的
v. （嗓音）颤抖；支吾；摇晃；踌躇；疲软；“falter”的现在分词
words.ex: The child took faltering steps on the ice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在冰上蹒跚地走着。
words.en: If you falter, you lose your confidence and stop doing something or start making mistakes.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 怀疑

words.ex: The fishy smell came from the old fish in the fridge.
words.ex_cn: 那股鱼腥味来自冰箱里的旧鱼。
words.en: If you describe something as fishy, you mean that it seems suspicious or dishonest.

words.tr:
n. 疑问；疑惑；
v. 怀疑；拿不准；
words.ex: I have doubt about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 我对这个答案有疑问。
words.en: If you have doubt or doubts about something, you feel uncertain about it and do not know whether it is true or possible. If you say that something is beyond doubt, you mean that it is definitely true.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.tr: n. 不信任；不轻信；怀疑
words.ex: He stared at her with incredulity when she said she won the lottery.
words.ex_cn: 当她说自己中了彩票时，他用不信任的眼神盯着她。
words.en: Incredulity is the state of being unwilling or unable to believe something.

words.tr:
n. 平衡；姿态；镇静
v. 使平衡；保持（某种姿势）
words.ex: The dancer maintained her poise on one foot.
words.ex_cn: 舞者单脚保持平衡。
words.en: If someone has poise, they are calm, dignified, and self-controlled.

words.ex: He is skeptical about the new plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新计划持怀疑态度。
words.en: If you are skeptical about something, you have doubts about it.

words.ex: I suspect it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我猜想明天会下雨。
words.en: If you suspect someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you believe that they have done it, although you have no proof.

words.ex: He looked at her with suspicion.
words.ex_cn: 他带着怀疑的眼神看着她。
words.en: A feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true, especially something bad or wrong, without having proof.

words.tr:
n. 怀疑；不信任
v. 怀疑；不信任
words.ex: He feels distrust toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 他不信任陌生人。
words.en: If you distrust someone or something, you think they are not honest, reliable, or safe.

words.ex: He stared at the money with disbelief.
words.ex_cn: 他难以置信地盯着那些钱。
words.en: Disbelief is the feeling of not being able to believe that something is true or real.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 愉悦

words.tr:
adj. 幸福的；受祝福的；神圣的
v. 祝福；保佑；“bless”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She is blessed with a kind heart.
words.ex_cn: 她拥有一颗善良的心。
words.en: Made holy; consecrated.

words.ex: She felt pure bliss when she held her newborn baby.
words.ex_cn: 当她抱住新生儿时，感受到了无上的幸福。
words.en: Bliss is a state of complete happiness.

words.ex: The sun brightens the room in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在早上使房间变亮。
words.en: To make something lighter or more colorful, or to make someone feel happier or more hopeful.

words.ex: He felt ecstasy after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品后感到无比喜悦。
words.en: Ecstasy is a feeling of very great happiness.

words.ex: There is a clear relation between exercise and health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼与健康之间有明显的关联。
words.en: A relation between two things is a connection or link between them.

words.ex: The music enraptured the whole audience.
words.ex_cn: 音乐让整个观众着迷。
words.en: To fill someone with great delight or joy.

words.tr:
adj. 高位的；高尚的；欣喜的
v. 赞扬；提升；加强；“exalt”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The exalted king sat on a golden throne.
words.ex_cn: 这位高位的国王坐在一张金宝座上。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as exalted, you mean they are at a high level of honor, rank, or quality.

words.ex: The children felt excitement before the birthday party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在生日派对前感到兴奋。
words.en: A feeling of great enthusiasm and eagerness.

words.ex: The crowd was exultant after their team won.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了之后，人群欣喜若狂。
words.en: If you are exultant, you feel very happy and proud because of something that has happened.

words.tr: adj. 愉快的；欣喜的；幸灾乐祸的
words.ex: The children were gleeful after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们赢了比赛后非常开心。
words.en: If you are gleeful, you are extremely happy and excited, often because something has happened that you wanted to happen.

words.ex: The movie was hilarious and made us laugh a lot.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影非常搞笑，让我们笑得很开心。
words.en: If you describe something as hilarious, you mean that it is extremely funny and it makes you laugh a lot.

words.tr: adj. 充满快乐的；使人高兴的
words.ex: The children were joyous on Christmas morning.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在圣诞节早上非常快乐。
words.en: If you describe something as joyous, you mean that it is full of joy and happiness.

words.tr: adj. 令人高兴的； v. “please”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pleasing smell of cookies made her smile.
words.ex_cn: 饼干令人高兴的香味让她笑了。
words.en: Something that is pleasing gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.tr:
n. 狂喜；非常高兴
v. 使…狂喜
words.ex: She felt rapture when she saw the sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到日出时，感到无比欣喜。
words.en: A feeling of intense pleasure or joy.

words.ex: The woman was ravished by a stranger.
words.ex_cn: 这名女子被一名陌生人强奸了。
words.en: If you are ravished by something, you are filled with delight and wonder by it.

words.ex: The children felt delight when they saw the toys.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到玩具时感到高兴。
words.en: Delight is a feeling of very great pleasure.

words.ex: He felt exhilaration after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后感到兴奋不已。
words.en: Exhilaration is a feeling of being very happy and excited.

words.tr:
adj. 喜气洋洋的；愉快的；耀眼的
v. 照耀；“beam”的现在分词
words.ex: She is beaming with joy after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 她赢得奖品后满脸喜悦。
words.en: If someone is beaming, they have a big smile on their face because they are happy, pleased, or proud about something.

words.ex: The children were blithesome playing in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里玩耍时非常快乐。
words.en: Someone who is blithesome is cheerful and has a light-hearted attitude.

chapters.name: Word List 33 心理 憎恨

words.ex: She abhors violence.
words.ex_cn: 她憎恶暴力。
words.en: If you abhor something, you hate it very much, especially because you think it is immoral or disgusting.

words.tr: adj. 可恶的；令人憎恶的；令人痛恨的
words.ex: He finds lying to friends abhorrent.
words.ex_cn: 他认为对朋友撒谎是令人厌恶的。
words.en: If something is abhorrent to you, you hate it very much, often because you think it is immoral or wrong.

words.ex: He has an aversion to spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他厌恶辛辣食物。
words.en: A strong dislike or disinclination towards someone or something.

words.ex: He detests eating broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌吃西兰花。
words.en: If you detest something, you dislike it intensely.

words.ex: He felt disgust when he saw the dirty food.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到脏兮兮的食物时，他感到厌恶。
words.en: A feeling of revulsion or profound disapproval aroused by something unpleasant or offensive.

words.tr:
n. 怨恨；积怨；嫌隙
v. 勉强做；不情愿地给；吝惜
words.ex: He holds a grudge against his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他对他哥哥心怀怨恨。
words.en: A grudge is a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury.

words.ex: He felt hatred for the man who hurt his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他憎恨那个伤害他兄弟的人。
words.en: Hatred is an extremely strong feeling of dislike for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 丑恶的；可怕的；丑陋的；
words.ex: The monster had a hideous face.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物有一张丑恶的脸。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is hideous, you mean that they are very ugly or unattractive.

words.ex: I loathe waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: If you loathe something or someone, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.tr: n. 憎恨；厌恶；可憎的事物
words.ex: The sight of the rotting food was an abomination.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的景象令人作呕。
words.en: An abomination is something that you dislike and disapprove of very strongly.

words.ex: He felt enmity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对他邻居怀有敌意。
words.en: Enmity is a feeling of hostility or ill will towards someone or something.

words.ex: She abominates cruelty to animals.
words.ex_cn: 她痛恨对动物的残忍行为。
words.en: If you abominate something, you hate it very much.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 帮助

words.ex: The school decided to adopt a new teaching method.
words.ex_cn: 学校决定采纳一种新的教学方法。
words.en: To adopt means to take up or start to use or follow (an idea, method, or course of action). It can also mean to legally take another's child and bring it up as one's own.

words.ex: He assists his brother with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助弟弟做作业。
words.en: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

words.ex: Eating vegetables is beneficial to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你的健康有益。
words.en: Promoting or enhancing well-being; advantageous.

words.tr:
v. 有益于；有助于；
n. 利益；好处；
words.ex: Exercise benefits your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼有益于你的健康。
words.en: A benefit is something that helps you or improves your life in some way.

words.ex: The benevolent man gave food to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这位慈善的人给穷人提供了食物。
words.en: If you describe a person in authority as benevolent, you mean that they are kind and fair.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈善事业的；
words.ex: She gave charitable donations to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 她向穷人捐赠了仁慈的善款。
words.en: A charitable organization or activity helps and supports people who are ill, very poor, or who have disabilities.

words.ex: The charity helps poor children get food and education.
words.ex_cn: 这个慈善团体帮助贫困儿童获得食物和教育。
words.en: An organization that helps people in need, or the act of giving money, food, or help to those who need it.

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.ex: He helped extricate the car from the mud.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助把车从泥里解脱出来。
words.en: If you extricate someone or something from a place where they are trapped or caught, you succeed in freeing them.

words.tr: adj. 有收益的；有报酬的；有利可图的
words.ex: He found a gainful job after graduation.
words.ex_cn: 他毕业后找到了一份有收入的工作。
words.en: Providing gain; profitable.

words.tr: adj. 有帮助的；乐器的；仪器的；
words.ex: Her advice was instrumental in helping me pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对帮助我通过考试很有帮助。
words.en: If someone or something is instrumental in a process, plan, or system, they are one of the most important influences in causing it to happen.

words.ex: The law obliges parents to send their children to school.
words.ex_cn: 法律责成父母送孩子上学。
words.en: If you describe someone as obliging, you mean that they are willing and eager to be helpful.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支柱；道具
v. 支撑；靠
words.ex: He uses a prop to support the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个道具来支撑架子。
words.en: A prop is an object or piece of furniture that is used in a play or film to make a scene look more realistic, or something that is used to support or hold up another object.

words.ex: The government must redress the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 政府必须纠正这部不公平的法律。
words.en: If you redress something such as a wrong or a complaint, you do something to correct it or to improve things for the person who has been wronged.

words.tr:
n. 救援；营救；
v. 救援；营救；
words.ex: The rescue came just in time to save the hikers.
words.ex_cn: 救援及时赶到，救出了徒步者。
words.en: To rescue someone or something means to save them from a dangerous or unpleasant situation.

words.tr:
n. 抢救；
v. 打捞；挽救；抢救；
words.ex: The salvage of the ship took three days.
words.ex_cn: 对这艘船的抢救花了三天时间。
words.en: To salvage something means to retrieve or preserve it from loss or destruction, especially from a shipwreck or fire. It can also refer to the act of saving or rescuing something from a difficult situation.

words.tr:
v. 节省；拯救；保存；
prep. 除...之外；除了；
words.ex: He saves money by walking to work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过步行上班来节省钱。
words.en: To save something means to keep it from being lost or damaged; to save money or time is to avoid spending more than necessary.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 保护

words.tr:
n. 护送；护航；护卫
v. 护航；护送
words.ex: The army sent a convoy to protect the trucks.
words.ex_cn: 军队派出护送队保护卡车。
words.en: A convoy is a group of vehicles or ships traveling together, typically accompanied by armed troops, warships, or other vehicles for protection.

words.ex: The soldiers defend their country from enemies.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们保卫自己的国家免受敌人入侵。
words.en: To defend means to protect someone or something from attack, harm, or criticism. It can also involve arguing in support of someone or something.

words.tr:
v. 护送；护卫
n. 护送者；护卫队
words.ex: He will escort her to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他将陪她去参加派对。
words.en: An escort is a person or vehicle that accompanies another person or vehicle, especially in order to provide protection or show them the way.

words.tr:
v. 保存；保护；保持；
n. （某群体）专有的活动；
words.ex: She preserves fresh fruit by making jam.
words.ex_cn: 她通过做果酱来保存新鲜水果。
words.en: To preserve something means to maintain it in its original or existing state.

words.ex: He retains his old photos in a box.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧照片保存在一个盒子里。
words.en: If you retain something, you keep it or continue to have it.

words.ex: The fence safeguards the garden from animals.
words.ex_cn: 围栏保护花园免受动物侵扰。
words.en: A safeguard is a measure taken to protect someone or something from potential harm or danger.

words.ex: The knight held up his shield to block the arrow.
words.ex_cn: 骑士举起盾牌来挡箭。
words.en: A shield is a piece of armor held in the hand or worn on the arm to protect the body from missiles or blows. It can also refer to something that protects or defends someone or something from harm or danger.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.ex: The helmet gives protection to his head.
words.ex_cn: 头盔保护他的头部。
words.en: Protection is the act of protecting someone or something, or the state of being protected.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 处理

words.ex: He abandoned his car in the snow.
words.ex_cn: 他把车抛弃在雪地里。
words.en: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave the place, thing, or person permanently or for a long time, especially when you should not do so.

words.ex: The school decided to adopt a new teaching method.
words.ex_cn: 学校决定采纳一种新的教学方法。
words.en: To adopt means to take up or start to use or follow (an idea, method, or course of action). It can also mean to legally take another's child and bring it up as one's own.

words.ex: I will arrange a meeting for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我将为明天安排一次会议。
words.en: If you arrange an event or meeting, you make plans for it to happen.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: He will cancel the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会取消会议。
words.en: If you cancel something that has been arranged, you stop it from happening. If you cancel an order for goods or services, you tell the person or organization supplying them that you no longer wish to receive them.

words.ex: He contrived to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他设法按时完成了项目。
words.en: If you contrive an event or situation, you succeed in making it happen, often by tricking someone.

words.tr:
v. 处理；对付；交易；
n. 交易；协议；
words.ex: He can deal with difficult problems easily.
words.ex_cn: 他能轻松处理困难的问题。
words.en: A deal is an agreement or arrangement, especially in business or politics, that is beneficial to all the parties involved.

words.ex: He will delete the old file.
words.ex_cn: 他会删除那个旧文件。
words.en: To delete something means to remove it or erase it.

words.tr:
v. 派遣；调遣；发送
n. 快信；发送；派遣
words.ex: He will dispatch the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会寄出这个包裹。
words.en: To send someone or something to a particular place for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: He disposed of the old books.
words.ex_cn: 他处理了那些旧书。
words.en: To dispose of something means to get rid of it, especially by throwing it away.

words.tr: v. 驱散；消散；浪费；挥霍
words.ex: The fog will dissipate by noon.
words.ex_cn: 雾将在中午前消散。
words.en: If something dissipates or is dissipated, it becomes less or becomes less strong until it disappears or goes away completely.

words.tr: v. 擦去；忘却；不抛头露面；使（自己）不受人注意
words.ex: He tried to efface the mark with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用橡皮擦掉那个痕迹。
words.en: To efface something means to remove it completely so that it no longer exists or is no longer noticeable.

words.ex: He will effectuate the plan next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周实施这个计划。
words.en: To effectuate something means to cause it to happen or to bring it about.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.ex: He erased the wrong answer with an eraser.
words.ex_cn: 他用橡皮擦掉了错误的答案。
words.en: To erase something means to remove it completely from a surface or from a place where it is stored.

words.ex: He exerted pressure on his team to win.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的团队施加了压力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To exert means to use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.

words.ex: He will not forsake his family.
words.ex_cn: 他不会抛弃他的家人。
words.en: If you forsake someone, you leave them when you should have stayed, or you stop helping them or looking after them.

words.ex: The old woman gleaned wheat from the field after the harvest.
words.ex_cn: 这位老妇人在收割后从田里拾落穗。
words.en: To gather information or material bit by bit.

words.tr:
v. 利用；
n. 马具；
words.ex: We must harness the power of the sun.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须利用太阳的能量。
words.en: A harness is a set of straps which fit under a person's arms and fasten round their body in order to keep a piece of equipment in place or to prevent the person moving from a place.

words.ex: The government will implement new rules next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将实施新规定。
words.en: To implement something means to ensure that what has been planned is done.

words.tr:
v. 丢弃；放弃；扔掉
n. 投弃；抛弃；投弃货物
words.ex: The pilot had to jettison extra fuel to land safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员不得不抛掉多余的燃料以安全着陆。
words.en: To jettison something means to throw it away or get rid of it, usually because it is not wanted or needed.

words.tr:
n. 工序；过程；
v. 处理；加工；
words.ex: The factory improved the production process.
words.ex_cn: 工厂改进了生产工序。
words.en: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

words.tr:
v. 净化；清除；清洗；整肃
n. 净化；清除；泻药
words.ex: The company purged its outdated systems.
words.ex_cn: 公司净化了其过时的系统。
words.en: To purge an organization or place of something or someone means to remove them from it because they are considered undesirable or harmful.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.tr:
n. 小块；碎片；废金属；吵架
v. 废弃；取消
adj. 废弃的
words.ex: He picked up a scrap of paper from the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起一张纸片。
words.en: A scrap is a small piece or amount of something, especially one that is left over after the greater part has been used. It can also mean to discard or get rid of something as being no longer useful or necessary.

words.tr:
n. 转移；移位；转变；轮班；
v. 变换位置；转移；换（挡）；轮班；
words.ex: The shift of power to the new government was sudden.
words.ex_cn: 权力向新政府的转移是突然的。
words.en: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves or changes its position slightly. If someone's opinion, attitude, or behaviour shifts, it changes slightly, especially in response to a particular situation or event.

words.ex: He will tackle the problem tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会处理这个问题。
words.en: If you tackle a problem or task, you deal with it in a determined way. In sports such as football and rugby, a tackle is an act of trying to take the ball from a player on the other team.

words.tr: v. 办理；交易；谈判；执行
words.ex: They transact business online every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天在线做生意。
words.en: If you transact business, you conduct business such as buying or selling goods or services.

words.ex: I clicked the button to undo my mistake.
words.ex_cn: 我点击了按钮来撤销我的错误。
words.en: To undo something means to reverse the effect of a previous action or to untie or unfasten something.

words.ex: We can utilize solar energy to power the house.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以利用太阳能来为房子供电。
words.en: To utilize something means to use it in a practical or effective way.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 促进

words.ex: The movie aroused his curiosity.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影激起了他的好奇心。
words.en: If something arouses a particular reaction or attitude in people, it causes them to have that reaction or attitude.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.ex: My teacher encourages me to speak English every day.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师鼓励我每天说英语。
words.en: If you encourage someone, you give them confidence, for example by letting them know that what they are doing is good and telling them that they should continue to do it.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.ex: He tries to foment trouble between the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在邻居之间挑起纠纷。
words.en: If someone foments trouble or violent opposition, they cause it to develop.

words.tr: v. 设防御工事；加强；增加营养物
words.ex: The soldiers fortify the hill with walls and trenches.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在山上用墙壁和战壕设防御工事。
words.en: To strengthen a place with defensive works so as to protect it against attack; to strengthen or invigorate someone mentally or physically.

words.tr:
adv. 进一步；更远；此外；
adj. 更多的；附加的；
v. 促进；
words.ex: He explained the problem, and then gave further examples.
words.ex_cn: 他解释了这个问题，然后给出了进一步的例子。
words.en: to a greater degree or extent

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.tr: adj. 凭冲动行事的；易冲动的
words.ex: He made an impulsive decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他一时冲动决定辞掉工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impulsive, you mean that they do things suddenly without thinking about them carefully first.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: Her story inspires me to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的故事激励我更加努力。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.ex: The storm will intensify tonight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴今晚会加强。
words.en: To make or become more intense or intensive.

words.tr: v. 点燃；生火；激起；发亮
words.ex: He used a match to kindle the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: To kindle something means to cause it to begin burning or to arouse or inspire it.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；激励；督促
n. 戳；刺；催促
words.ex: He prodded the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke or jab someone or something, often with a finger or a pointed object, in order to get their attention or to encourage them to do something.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: The wind propels the sailboat forward.
words.ex_cn: 风推动帆船前进。
words.en: To propel something in a particular direction means to cause it to move in that direction.

words.tr:
n. 鞭策；
v. 刺激；
words.ex: The competition served as a spur to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 竞争成了推动他更努力工作的鞭策。
words.en: A spur is something that makes you want to do something or that encourages you to do it. It can also refer to a sharp device worn on the heel of a rider's boot to urge a horse forward.

words.ex: The bright light stimulated her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 强烈的光线刺激了她的眼睛。
words.en: To stimulate something means to encourage it to begin or develop further.

words.tr:
v. 力劝；
n. 强烈欲望；
words.ex: My teacher urged me to study harder.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师力劝我更加努力学习。
words.en: If you urge someone to do something, you try hard to persuade them to do it.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 获得

words.ex: His attainment of the goal took many years.
words.ex_cn: 他达到这个目标花了多年时间。
words.en: The act of achieving something, especially through effort; a skill or accomplishment that has been achieved.

words.ex: He obtained a new job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周获得了一份新工作。
words.en: If you obtain something, you get it or achieve it.

words.tr:
v. 获得；增加；
n. 增益；获得；
words.ex: He gained a new skill last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月获得了一项新技能。
words.en: To gain means to obtain something that is useful, that gives you an advantage, or that is in some way positive, especially over a period of time.

words.tr: v. 弥补；兑换；付清；赎回；履行
words.ex: He worked hard to redeem his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作来弥补自己的错误。
words.en: To redeem something means to get it back by paying a sum of money or by doing something to compensate for a fault or mistake.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.tr: n. 恢复；重新开始；继续进行
words.ex: The resumption of classes was delayed by one week.
words.ex_cn: 课程的恢复被推迟了一周。
words.en: The act of starting something again after a pause or interruption.

words.ex: He tries to procure food for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他努力为家人获取食物。
words.en: To obtain something, especially with care or effort.

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.ex: Graduating with honors was her greatest accomplishment.
words.ex_cn: 以优异成绩毕业是她最大的成就。
words.en: Something that has been achieved successfully.

words.tr: vt. 收回；取复；重新获得
words.ex: The bank will repossess the car if he misses payments.
words.ex_cn: 如果他未能付款，银行将收回这辆车。
words.en: To take back possession of something, especially property, because payments have not been made.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 躲避

words.ex: He avoids eating sugar to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他避免吃糖以保持健康。
words.en: If you avoid something, you take action in order to prevent it from happening to you.

words.tr:
v. 避开；躲避
n. 躲避；诡计
words.ex: He dodged the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速躲开了球。
words.en: If you dodge, you move quickly, often to avoid being hit, caught, or seen.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.tr:
v. 逃避；逃走；
n. 逃脱；逃避；
words.ex: He tried to escape from the prison.
words.ex_cn: 他试图逃离监狱。
words.en: To escape means to get away from a place or a situation that you are in, especially because it is difficult or dangerous to stay there.

words.ex: He tries to eschew sugar for health reasons.
words.ex_cn: 他为了健康尽量避免吃糖。
words.en: If you eschew something, you deliberately avoid doing it or becoming involved in it.

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: He tried evasion to avoid paying taxes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图逃避缴税。
words.en: The act of avoiding something that you are supposed to do or deal with.

words.tr: adj. 逃避的；推托的；闪烁其辞的
words.ex: He gave an evasive answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个回避的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as evasive, you mean that they deliberately avoid giving clear direct answers to questions.

words.ex: He shuns loud parties because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而避开热闹的派对。
words.en: If you shun someone or something, you deliberately avoid them or keep away from them.

words.tr: adj. 诡诈的；诡秘的；心照不宣的
words.ex: The sly fox stole the chicken at night.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸在夜里偷了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is sly is clever and good at deceiving people in a way that is not easily noticed.

words.ex: He shirks his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天逃避作业。
words.en: If someone shirks their duties or responsibilities, they deliberately avoid doing them.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 反抗

words.ex: The defiant child refused to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 这个不顺从的孩子拒绝打扫房间。
words.en: If you say that someone is defiant, you mean they show aggression or independence by refusing to obey someone.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.tr:
v. 提出异议；表示反对
n. 异议；反对
words.ex: He demurred when asked to sign the contract.
words.ex_cn: 当被要求签署合同时，他提出了异议。
words.en: If you demur, you express reluctance or objection to something.

words.ex: The student was insubordinate to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这名学生对老师不服从。
words.en: If someone is insubordinate, they deliberately do not obey someone of higher rank.

words.tr: adj. 反对的；敌对的； v. 反对；反抗；“oppose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was opposed to the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这个新规定。
words.en: If you are opposed to something, you disagree with it or disapprove of it.

words.ex: The rebellion against the king failed.
words.ex_cn: 反对国王的叛乱失败了。
words.en: A rebellion is an organized attempt to overthrow a government or authority by a group of people.

words.ex: He tried to resist the temptation to eat sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抵制吃甜食的诱惑。
words.en: If you resist something such as a change, you refuse to accept it and try to prevent it.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.tr:
v. 叛乱；反叛；（使）厌恶
n. 叛乱；厌恶；反感
words.ex: The people revolt against the unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 人们反抗不公平的规则。
words.en: If a large number of people revolt, they refuse to be controlled or ruled, and take action against authority, often violent action.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.ex: The company developed a countermeasure to combat the new security threat.
words.ex_cn: 公司制定了一项对策来应对新的安全威胁。
words.en: A countermeasure is an action or strategy that is intended to counteract or offset another action or situation.

words.tr: adj. 不服从的；违背的；不孝的
words.ex: The child was disobedient and refused to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子不听话，拒绝打扫房间。
words.en: If someone is disobedient, they deliberately do not do what someone in authority tells them to do, or what a rule or law says they should do.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.ex: The mutinous crew refused to follow the captain's orders.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱的船员拒绝服从船长的命令。
words.en: If someone is mutinous, they are strongly dissatisfied with a person in authority and are likely to stop obeying them.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 否定

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.ex: He denies taking the money.
words.ex_cn: 他否认拿了钱。
words.en: To deny means to declare that something is not true, or to refuse to give or grant something.

words.tr: v. 否认；放弃；拒绝承认
words.ex: He disclaims any responsibility for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他否认对这个错误负有任何责任。
words.en: If you disclaim knowledge of something or disclaim responsibility for something, you say that you did not know about it or are not responsible for it.

words.tr: n. 排除；排斥；被排除在外的事物；
words.ex: The exclusion of students from the test was unfair.
words.ex_cn: 将学生排除在考试之外是不公平的。
words.en: The act of preventing someone or something from entering a place or taking part in an activity.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.ex: He had to relinquish his seat to an old man.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不把座位让给一位老人。
words.en: If you relinquish something, such as power or control, you give it up, often unwillingly.

words.tr: v. 声明放弃；与...断绝关系
words.ex: He renounced his citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年放弃了国籍。
words.en: If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you say and show that you no longer hold that belief or will behave in that way.

words.ex: His denial of the mistake made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他否认错误，让所有人都生气了。
words.en: A denial is a statement that something is not true or does not exist.

words.ex: He gave a disavowal of the false statement.
words.ex_cn: 他否认了那句虚假的言论。
words.en: A disavowal is a statement in which you say that you are not responsible for something, or that you do not agree with or support something.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.ex: The judge will overrule the objection.
words.ex_cn: 法官将驳回这个异议。
words.en: If someone in authority overrules a decision or order, they officially decide that it is wrong and change it.

words.tr:
n. 否决；否决权
v. 否决
words.ex: The president used his veto to stop the law.
words.ex_cn: 总统行使否决权阻止了这项法律。
words.en: If someone in authority vetoes something, they forbid it, or they stop it from being put into action.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 服从

words.ex: He will defer his trip until next month.
words.ex_cn: 他将把旅行推迟到下个月。
words.en: If you defer an event or action, you arrange for it to happen at a later date, rather than immediately or at the previously planned time.

words.ex: The magic show enthralls the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们着迷。
words.en: If you are enthralled by something, you are so interested and excited by it that you give it all your attention.

words.ex: The child showed obedience to his parents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对父母表现出顺从。
words.en: Obedience is the act of following orders or instructions from someone in authority.

words.ex: The subjection of the people to the law is important.
words.ex_cn: 人民对法律的服从很重要。
words.en: The act of subjecting or the state of being subjected, especially to control or authority.

words.ex: His submission to the boss ended the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板的屈服结束了这场冲突。
words.en: The act of submitting something to someone for their decision or consideration; the state of being submissive or obedient.

words.tr: adj. 顺从的；服从的；恭顺的；
words.ex: The submissive dog waited quietly for its owner's command.
words.ex_cn: 这只顺从的狗安静地等待主人的命令。
words.en: If you are submissive, you obey someone without arguing.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.ex: He succumbed to the illness after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 经过长期抗争后，他最终死于疾病。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or something such as an illness, you do something that you want to do, or you give in to the pressure or illness, often after a period of trying not to.

words.ex: The company showed compliance with safety rules.
words.ex_cn: 该公司遵守了安全规定。
words.en: The act of complying with a wish, request, or demand; obedience.

words.ex: He showed deference to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他对老师表示尊敬。
words.en: Deference is a polite and respectful attitude towards someone, often because they are older or more experienced than you.

words.ex: He gave his acquiescence to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他默许了这个计划。
words.en: Acquiescence is the act of accepting or agreeing to something without protest.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 负面行为

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.ex: She coddles her little brother too much.
words.ex_cn: 她太宠着她的弟弟了。
words.en: To treat someone in an indulgent or overprotective way.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.tr: v. 把…强加给；使遭受；使承受
words.ex: The storm inflicted heavy damage on the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给村庄造成了严重破坏。
words.en: If you inflict something unpleasant on someone, you make them suffer it.

words.tr:
n. 闪光；一刹那；
v. 闪光；闪现；
words.ex: The camera captured a sudden flash of light.
words.ex_cn: 相机捕捉到了一道突然的闪光。
words.en: A flash is a sudden bright light that quickly disappears. As a verb, it means to shine brightly for a short time or to appear or pass suddenly.

words.tr:
v. 使堕落；误用；歪曲；使走邪路
n. 堕落者；性变态者；色狼
words.ex: He tried to pervert the truth with lies.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用谎言歪曲真相。
words.en: If you pervert something, you change it from what it should be or what it was originally intended to be into something that is wrong or harmful.

words.ex: The child suffered maltreatment from his caregiver.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子受到了照顾者的虐待。
words.en: Maltreatment is cruel or violent treatment of someone.

words.ex: The exploitation of natural resources helps the economy grow.
words.ex_cn: 自然资源的开发有助于经济发展。
words.en: The action or fact of treating someone unfairly in order to benefit from their work, or the utilization of something for profit or gain.

words.ex: Parents shouldn't indulge their children's bad habits.
words.ex_cn: 父母不应该放任孩子的坏习惯。
words.en: To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to have something enjoyable, especially more than is good for you.

words.tr: v. 损毁…的外形；使变丑
words.ex: The accident disfigured his face.
words.ex_cn: 那次事故使他的脸变形了。
words.en: To disfigure someone or something means to spoil their appearance.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 改良

words.tr: v. 调整；使适合；使适应；
words.ex: He adjusted the chair to sit comfortably.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了椅子以便坐得舒服。
words.en: To adjust something means to change it so that it is more effective or appropriate, or so that it fits better.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.tr:
adj. 正确的；
v. 改正；修正；
words.ex: The answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 这个答案是正确的。
words.en: If something is correct, it is right and true. If you correct someone, you tell them that they are wrong.

words.ex: She embellished the dress with flowers.
words.ex_cn: 她用花朵装饰了这条裙子。
words.en: To embellish something means to make it more attractive by adding decorative details or features.

words.tr: v. 刺绣；绣（花）；加以渲染（或润色）
words.ex: She embroiders flowers on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上刺绣花朵。
words.en: To embroider means to decorate cloth or other material by sewing patterns or pictures on it with colored threads.

words.tr:
v. （在食物上）加装饰菜；装饰
n. （食物上的）装饰菜；装饰
words.ex: She puts a lemon slice to garnish the drink.
words.ex_cn: 她放一片柠檬来装饰这杯饮料。
words.en: To garnish something means to decorate it with something, especially food with small amounts of different foods.

words.ex: He tried to gild the old box with gold paint.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用金漆把旧盒子镀金。
words.en: To cover something with a thin layer of gold or to make something seem more attractive or valuable than it really is.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.ex: He will mend his broken shoe.
words.ex_cn: 他将修补他破掉的鞋子。
words.en: If you mend something that is broken or damaged, you repair it, so that it works properly or so that it looks like new again.

words.ex: The modification improved the design.
words.ex_cn: 这个修改改进了设计。
words.en: A modification is a change or alteration made to something to improve it or to make it suitable for a different purpose.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He modulates his voice to sound calm.
words.ex_cn: 他调节自己的声音以显得平静。
words.en: To modulate means to change or adjust something, such as your voice or a piece of equipment, to achieve a desired effect or to make it suitable for a particular situation.

words.ex: The tree has many colorful ornaments.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树上有许多彩色的装饰品。
words.en: An ornament is an object that is used to make something look more attractive but is usually considered to have no practical purpose.

words.ex: He refines his writing every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天完善自己的写作。
words.en: To refine something means to make it purer or to improve it, especially by removing unwanted substances or by making small changes.

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 干涉

words.tr:
v. 畏缩不前；犹豫；妨碍
n. 阻碍，妨碍
words.ex: He balks at paying high prices.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意支付高价。
words.en: If you balk at something, you hesitate to do it or agree to it, often because it is unpleasant or difficult.

words.tr:
n. 路障；栅栏；阻碍
v. 设路障；阻挡
words.ex: The police put up a barricade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察设了一个路障来阻止人群。
words.en: A barricade is a temporary structure that is built across a road, entrance, or other route to prevent people from passing. It can also refer to the act of creating such a structure.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.tr:
n. 大楼；大厦；块；街区；障碍物；
v. 阻塞；阻碍；
words.ex: The new block is next to the park.
words.ex_cn: 这栋新大楼就在公园旁边。
words.en: A block is a large solid piece of material with flat surfaces on each side. As a verb, to block means to prevent movement or progress.

words.tr:
n. 厚木底皮鞋；木屐
v. 堵塞；妨碍
words.ex: She wore wooden clogs to work in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着厚木底皮鞋去花园干活。
words.en: If something clogs a hole or place, it blocks it so that nothing can pass through.

words.ex: He gave a conciliatory smile to calm the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他露出和解的微笑来平息争执。
words.en: If you are conciliatory, you show that you are willing to end a disagreement with someone by doing or saying things that will please them.

words.ex: He is encumbered by too many debts.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的债务拖累。
words.en: To encumber someone or something means to weigh them down or to block or hinder them.

words.tr:
n. 箔；陪衬物
v. 阻止；挫败
words.ex: He used foil to wrap the sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他用锡纸包住了三明治。
words.en: To prevent someone from succeeding in their plans or intentions, especially by doing something clever or unexpected.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr:
v. 阻碍；妨碍
n. （带盖）篮子
words.ex: Rain hampered our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨妨碍了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If something hampers you, it makes it difficult for you to do something.

words.tr:
n. 残疾；障碍；阻碍；不利
v. 妨碍；使不利
words.ex: He has a physical handicap but still runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 他有身体残疾，但仍然每天跑步。
words.en: A handicap is a condition that markedly restricts a person's ability to function physically, mentally, or socially.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.tr:
n. 跨栏；障碍；难关
v. 越过障碍；克服
words.ex: He jumped over the hurdle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速跳过了跨栏。
words.en: A hurdle is a problem or difficulty that you must deal with before you can achieve something.

words.ex: The injury incapacitated him for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他几周无法行动。
words.en: To make someone unable to do something, especially because of injury or illness.

words.ex: He will intercede for his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他会为他的朋友出面说情。
words.en: If you intercede with someone, you try to persuade them to forgive someone or end their disagreement with them.

words.ex: The police intercepted the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察拦截了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If you intercept someone or something that is going from one place to another, you stop them before they get there.

words.ex: Don't interfere when I am working.
words.ex_cn: 我工作时不要打扰。
words.en: To interfere means to involve oneself in a situation where one is not wanted or needed, often causing problems or hindering progress.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: Don't meddle in my affairs.
words.ex_cn: 别插手我的事情。
words.en: To meddle means to interfere in something that is not one's concern.

words.ex: He tries to mediate between the two friends.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在两个朋友之间调解。
words.en: To intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: The big rock was an obstacle on the road.
words.ex_cn: 那块大石头是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstacle is something which makes it difficult for you to go forward or to achieve something.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet can prevent head injuries.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔可以防止头部受伤。
words.en: To prevent something means to stop it from happening or to stop someone from doing something.

words.tr:
n. 小困难或障碍；划破处；钩丝处
v. 被钩住；划破；抢先获得
words.ex: He found a snag in the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他在计划中发现了一个问题。
words.en: A snag is a small problem or difficulty that you did not expect.

words.tr: n. 特技表演；噱头；发育不良的动植物；
words.ex: The actor performed a dangerous stunt in the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员在电影中表演了一个危险的特技。
words.en: A stunt is a dangerous feat that is done to entertain people, especially in a film.

words.tr: v. 拨弄；玩弄；篡改；收买
words.ex: Don't tamper with the machine.
words.ex_cn: 不要拨弄这台机器。
words.en: If someone tampers with something, they interfere with it or make unauthorized changes to it, often in order to cause damage or make it work differently.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 跟踪

words.tr: v. 以网或陷阱捕捉；俘获；诱获；诱捕
words.ex: The hunter used a net to entrap the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猎人用网捕捉了那只鸟。
words.en: To catch someone or something in a trap or to trick someone into doing something they would not normally do.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.tr:
n. 痕迹；轨迹；微量；
v. 追踪；追溯；仔细查找；
words.ex: There was no trace of blood on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 地板上没有血迹。
words.en: If you trace something such as a pattern or a shape, you draw it carefully over a piece of thin paper. You can also trace someone or something that is missing or has disappeared, by following their movements or actions.

words.ex: The old house has a vestige of its original design.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子还保留着它原始设计的痕迹。
words.en: A vestige is a small part or amount of something that remains after the rest has disappeared or been destroyed.

words.tr:
n. 侦察兵；
v. 搜寻；
words.ex: The scout watched the enemy's movement quietly.
words.ex_cn: 侦察兵悄悄观察敌人的动向。
words.en: A scout is someone who is sent to an area of countryside to find out the position of an enemy or to search for a suitable place for a military camp.

words.tr:
n. 踪迹；轨道；小路；跑道；
v. 追踪；跟踪；
words.ex: The dog followed the track of the rabbit.
words.ex_cn: 狗跟着兔子的踪迹。
words.en: A track is a path or route along which something moves or travels. It can also refer to marks left by something that has passed, or the act of following such marks to find someone or something.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 固定

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支架；牙箍
v. 支撑；绷紧；紧靠；准备好
words.ex: The old bookshelf needs a brace to stay steady.
words.ex_cn: 旧书架需要一个支撑物来保持稳定。
words.en: To brace oneself means to prepare oneself for something difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 固定的；不能变的； v. 修理；固定；确定；“fix”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He has a fixed schedule every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都有一个固定的日程。
words.en: If something is fixed, it is attached or positioned so that it cannot move, or is arranged in a particular way and cannot be changed.

words.ex: He will fix the broken chair tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会修理那把坏掉的椅子。
words.en: To fix something means to repair it, to make it firm or stable, or to arrange or decide it.

words.ex: The injured man was immobile after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，这名受伤的人无法移动。
words.en: If something is immobile, it is not moving or cannot move.

words.ex: He will install the new software on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他将在他的电脑上安装新软件。
words.en: To set up or fix in position for use or service.

words.tr:
v. 设置；使固定；放置；
n. 一组；一套；
adj. 固定的；位于…的；安排好的；
words.ex: He set the alarm for 6 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他把闹钟设在早上六点。
words.en: To put something in a specified place or position; to adjust or arrange something; a group of things that belong together or are used together; fixed or established.

words.ex: The chair is stationary and does not move.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是固定的，不会移动。
words.en: not moving or not intended to be moved

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 观察

words.ex: I can detect a change in her mood.
words.ex_cn: 我能察觉到她情绪的变化。
words.en: To detect something means to find it or discover it, often using special equipment or methods.

words.ex: The error is detectable with a simple test.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误可以通过简单的测试检测出来。
words.en: If something is detectable, it can be noticed or discovered.

words.ex: The difference is discernible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个差异肉眼可见。
words.en: able to be discerned; perceptible

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.ex: His insight helped the team solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的洞察力帮助团队解决了问题。
