words.en: If you gain insight or an insight into a complex situation or problem, you gain an accurate and deep understanding of it.

words.ex: The police will investigate the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方将调查这起事故。
words.en: If someone, especially an official, investigates an event, situation, or claim, they try to find out what happened or what is the truth.

words.tr: v. 确定…的位置；使坐落于；查找…的地点；
words.ex: Can you locate the hotel on the map?
words.ex_cn: 你能在地图上找到酒店的位置吗？
words.en: To locate something means to find out exactly where it is, or to establish something in a particular place.

words.tr: n. 观察；观测；注意；监视；(观察后的）意见；
words.ex: The scientist made an observation about the bird's behavior.
words.ex_cn: 科学家对这只鸟的行为进行了观察。
words.en: The act of noticing or watching something carefully in order to gain information.

words.ex: The scientist observe the birds every morning.
words.ex_cn: 科学家每天早上观察鸟类。
words.en: If you observe a person or thing, you watch them carefully, especially in order to learn something about them.

words.ex: I perceive a change in his mood.
words.ex_cn: 我察觉到他的情绪有变化。
words.en: If you perceive something, you see, notice, or realize it, especially when it is not obvious.

words.tr: adj. 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perceptive and notices small changes.
words.ex_cn: 她很有洞察力，能注意到细微的变化。
words.en: If you describe someone as perceptive, you mean that they are good at noticing or understanding things.

words.tr: n. 视角；观点；（对事物的）合理判断；
words.ex: His perspective on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的看法非常积极。
words.en: A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.tr: v. 详细检查；仔细察看
words.ex: The teacher scrutinizes every student's homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细检查每位学生的作业。
words.en: If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 坚持

words.ex: He showed great fortitude during the hard times.
words.ex_cn: 他在艰难时期展现了极大的毅力。
words.en: Fortitude is the mental and emotional strength that enables a person to face difficulty, danger, or pain without fear.

words.tr: adj. 不屈不挠的；百折不挠的
words.ex: He is indomitable in facing challenges.
words.ex_cn: 他在面对挑战时永不言败。
words.en: If you say that someone has an indomitable spirit, you admire them because they never give up or admit that they have been defeated.

words.ex: The rules are inflexible and cannot be changed.
words.ex_cn: 这些规则是不灵活的，不能更改。
words.en: If you say that someone is inflexible, you are criticizing them because they refuse to change their mind or alter their way of doing things.

words.ex: She insists on going home now.
words.ex_cn: 她坚决要求现在回家。
words.en: If you insist on doing something, you keep doing it, even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.tr: adj. 不能调和的；无法化解的；不兼容的
words.ex: Their views are irreconcilable.
words.ex_cn: 他们的观点无法调和。
words.en: If two things such as opinions or proposals are irreconcilable, they are so different from each other that it is not possible to believe or have both of them.

words.tr:
n. 辩论；讨论；
v. 辩论；讨论；
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: If you maintain something, you continue to have it, and do not let it stop or grow weaker.

words.ex: His perseverance helped him finish the marathon.
words.ex_cn: 他的毅力帮助他完成了马拉松。
words.en: Perseverance is the quality of continuing to try to achieve a particular aim despite difficulties.

words.ex: He persevered despite many failures.
words.ex_cn: 尽管多次失败，他仍然坚持不懈。
words.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

words.ex: He made a persistent effort to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他持续努力学习英语。
words.en: Continuing firmly or obstinately in a course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition.

words.ex: He tried to resist the temptation to eat sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抵制吃甜食的诱惑。
words.en: If you resist something such as a change, you refuse to accept it and try to prevent it.

words.tr: adj. 坚决的；毅然的；有决心的；
words.ex: He was resolute in his decision to quit smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他决心戒烟。
words.en: If you describe someone as resolute, you approve of them because they are very determined not to change their mind or not to give up a course of action.

words.ex: He is steadfast in his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念坚定不移。
words.en: If someone is steadfast, they are very loyal and constant in their attitudes or actions.

words.tr: adv. 坚忍地；恬淡寡欲地
words.ex: He stoically accepted the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 他平静地接受了这个坏消息。
words.en: In a manner that endures pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining.

words.ex: The table is made of sturdy wood.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是用坚固的木头做的。
words.en: Someone or something that is sturdy looks strong and is unlikely to be easily injured or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.tr: adj. 不动摇的；坚决的；泰然自若的
words.ex: He remained unshaken after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他依然坚定不移。
words.en: If you describe someone's belief or attitude as unshaken, you mean that it is strong and firm and not likely to be weakened.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 顽固

words.tr: adj. 固执己见的；偏执的；执迷的
words.ex: He is bigoted and refuses to listen to others.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝听取别人的意见。
words.en: If you describe someone as bigoted, you mean that they are bigoted.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；固执的；顽固的；
words.ex: He is obstinate and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很执拗，不肯改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obstinate, you are being critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.tr: adj. 讲究实际的；头脑清晰的；不感情用事的
words.ex: He is hardheaded and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as hardheaded, you mean that they are practical and determined to get what they want, and do not let emotions or other people's opinions affect them.

words.tr: adj. 刚愎自用的；顽固的；任性的
words.ex: He is headstrong and refuses to listen.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不肯听别人的话。
words.en: If you refer to someone as headstrong, you are slightly critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to be advised by others.

words.ex: He is mulish and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as mulish, you mean they are determined to do what they want to do and will not change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.tr: adj. 固执己见的；顽固的
words.ex: He is opinionated and never changes his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很有主见，从不改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as opinionated, you mean that they have very strong opinions and refuse to accept that they may be wrong.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的，愚蠢的；固执的
words.ex: He is pigheaded and won't listen to anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不肯听任何人的话。
words.en: If you describe someone as pigheaded, you mean that they are unreasonably stubborn and refuse to change their mind or consider other people's opinions.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 揭示

words.ex: The tree has bare branches in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树在冬天有光秃秃的树枝。
words.en: If part of your body is bare, it is not covered by any clothing.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.ex: The symbol x denotes an unknown number.
words.ex_cn: 符号 x 表示一个未知数。
words.en: If one thing denotes another, it is a sign or indication of it.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.ex: The museum will exhibit ancient coins next month.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆下个月将展览古钱币。
words.en: To exhibit something means to show it in a public place so that people can go to see it. It can also mean to show a particular quality, ability, or type of behavior.

words.ex: The children were exposed to cold weather without coats.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在没有外套的情况下遭受了寒冷天气。
words.en: To expose something means to uncover it so that it can be seen, or to make it known or public.

words.ex: The worker had long exposure to loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人长期暴露在噪音中。
words.en: The condition of being exposed to something, especially to something harmful or unpleasant.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.ex: The dark clouds indicate rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云表明要下雨了。
words.en: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.

words.tr:
n. 漏洞；泄露；
v. 漏；泄露；
words.ex: The leak in the roof caused water to drip inside.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶的漏洞导致水滴进屋里。
words.en: If a container or pipe leaks, or if it leaks a substance such as liquid or gas, the substance comes out of it accidentally because there is a hole or crack in it.

words.tr: v. 公开承认；宣布；声称
words.ex: He professes to love music.
words.ex_cn: 他声称自己热爱音乐。
words.en: If you profess to do or have something, you claim that you do it or have it.

words.tr: n. 沉思；反射；反映；反省；
words.ex: He sat quietly in the garden for reflection.
words.ex_cn: 他静静地坐在花园里沉思。
words.en: A reflection is an image that you can see in a mirror, glass, or water.

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr: n. 揭露；被揭示的真相；
words.ex: The letter was a revelation about his secret life.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他隐秘的生活。
words.en: A revelation is a surprising and previously unknown fact that has been disclosed to others.

words.tr:
v. 展示；表明；给...看；
n. 节目；演出；展览会；表现；
words.ex: He shows his photos to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友们展示他的照片。
words.en: To show something means to make it visible or to allow it to be seen. It can also refer to a performance or exhibition intended to entertain or educate.

words.ex: The red light signifies stop.
words.ex_cn: 红灯表示停止。
words.en: If an event, a sign, or a symbol signifies something, it is a sign of that thing or represents that thing.

words.tr: v. 蒸发；排出；为人所知；发生
words.ex: Water transpires from the leaves in hot weather.
words.ex_cn: 水在炎热的天气中从叶子中蒸发。
words.en: If it transpires that something has happened, this previously secret or unknown fact becomes known.

words.tr: v. 摘下面纱；揭幕；揭露
words.ex: They will unveil the statue tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将摘下雕像的面纱。
words.en: If someone unveils something such as a new statue or painting, they show it to the public for the first time.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 思考

words.ex: He was conscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后他醒了过来。
words.en: If you are conscious of something, you notice it or are aware of it.

words.ex: I consider going to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我考虑明天去公园。
words.en: If you consider something, you think about it carefully.

words.tr: adj. 考虑周到的；体贴的；
words.ex: He is considerate and always asks if others need help.
words.ex_cn: 他很体贴，总是问别人是否需要帮助。
words.en: Someone who is considerate pays attention to the needs, wishes, or feelings of other people.

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.tr: vt. 铭记于心；使不朽；防腐；使充满香气
words.ex: They embalm the memory of their hero.
words.ex_cn: 他们铭记着英雄的记忆。
words.en: To embalm a dead body means to treat it with special substances to prevent it from decaying.

words.ex: The memory of the accident still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故的记忆仍然长期困扰着他。
words.en: If something unpleasant haunts you, you keep thinking or worrying about it over a long period of time. A place that is haunted is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.ex: He sat in a meditative pose by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在湖边，摆出沉思冥想的姿势。
words.en: A meditative state or process involves deep thought or concentration, often as part of a religious or spiritual practice.

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.tr:
v. 回忆起；召回；
n. 记忆力；
words.ex: I recall my first day at school.
words.ex_cn: 我想起了我上学的第一天。
words.en: If you recall something, you remember it and tell others about it.

words.ex: He smiled at the recollection of his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他回忆起童年时微笑了。
words.en: The act of remembering something or the ability to remember.

words.ex: He sits quietly to ruminate on his choices.
words.ex_cn: 他静静地坐着沉思自己的选择。
words.en: To ruminate means to think deeply about something or to chew the cud, as a cow does.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.ex: The baby ate the tender broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃了嫩的西兰花。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as tender, you mean that they are kind, gentle, and sympathetic. If meat or other food is tender, it is easy to cut or chew. To tender something such as a service or a resignation means to formally offer or present it.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 控制

words.tr:
v. 处理；操纵；
n. 把手；柄；
words.ex: He can handle difficult problems easily.
words.ex_cn: 他能轻松处理难题。
words.en: To deal with or control a situation or problem.

words.ex: Her irrepressible laugh filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 她抑制不住的笑声充满了房间。
words.en: If someone is irrepressible, they are full of energy and enthusiasm and cannot be controlled or stopped.

words.tr: v. 运转；操作；施行手术；
words.ex: The machine operates smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器运转顺畅。
words.en: If you operate a business or organization, you work to keep it running properly. If a business or organization operates, it carries out its work.

words.tr: adj. 不守规矩的；难控制的；难管束的
words.ex: The unruly child refused to sit quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这个不守规矩的孩子不肯安静地坐着。
words.en: If you describe people, especially children, as unruly, you mean that they behave badly and are difficult to control.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.tr: v. 占主导地位；占支配地位；
words.ex: English predominate in this region.
words.ex_cn: 英语在这个地区占主导地位。
words.en: If one type of person or thing predominates in a group, there is more of that type than of any other.

words.tr:
n. 缰绳；驾驭；控制
v. 控制；驾驭
words.ex: He uses a leather rein to control the horse.
words.ex_cn: 他用皮缰绳来控制马。
words.en: A rein is a long, narrow strap attached at one end to a horse's bit, typically used in pairs to guide or check a horse while riding or driving.

words.tr: v. 给予（药物或治疗）；管理；实施；
words.ex: The nurse will administer the medicine to the patient.
words.ex_cn: 护士会给病人服药。
words.en: To administer means to manage or oversee the execution, use, or conduct of something; to dispense or apply (a remedy or drug).

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 理解

words.ex: He cannot comprehend the simple math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他无法理解这个简单的数学问题。
words.en: To comprehend something means to understand it fully.

words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: It is evident that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is evident, it is easy to see, perceive, or understand.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.tr:
v. 领会；抓紧；
n. 领会；
words.ex: I couldn't grasp the meaning of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 我没能领会这首诗的含义。
words.en: To grasp something means to take it in your hand and hold it firmly.

words.ex: His ignorance of the rules caused the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的无知导致了这个错误。
words.en: Lack of knowledge or information.

words.tr: adj. 无知的；缺乏知识的
words.ex: He was ignorant of the basic rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对基本规则一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as ignorant, you mean that they do not know things they should know. If someone is ignorant of a fact, they do not know it.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: The mysterious box appeared on his doorstep.
words.ex_cn: 那个神秘的盒子出现在他的门口。
words.en: If someone or something is mysterious, it is not fully understood or explained and seems interesting or puzzling.

words.ex: I couldn't apprehend the math lesson because it was too fast.
words.ex_cn: 我无法理解这节数学课，因为讲得太快了。
words.en: If the police apprehend someone, they catch them and arrest them.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 掠夺

words.ex: The storm bereaved the village of its power.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴使村庄失去了电力。
words.en: To deprive someone of a loved one through death.

words.tr: v. 不断骚扰；打扰；侵扰；
words.ex: The neighbors harry the old man with loud music every night.
words.ex_cn: 邻居们每晚用吵闹的音乐不断骚扰那位老人。
words.en: To harry someone means to repeatedly attack them or to cause them problems.

words.tr:
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
v. 掠夺；洗劫
words.ex: The pirates found loot on the sunken ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗们在沉船中找到了战利品。
words.en: Loot refers to goods stolen from a place, especially during a war or riot. It can also mean to steal goods from a place, especially during a war or riot.

words.tr: adj. 贪婪的；贪得无厌的；劫掠的
words.ex: The rapacious wolf ate all the food.
words.ex_cn: 贪婪的狼吃掉了所有食物。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as rapacious, you disapprove of their greedy or selfish behaviour.

words.tr:
v. 毁坏；破坏；劫掠
n. 破坏；蹂躏
words.ex: The storm ravaged the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个小村庄。
words.en: To ravage means to cause severe and extensive damage to something.

words.tr:
n. 长条；条状；
v. 剥去；剥夺；
words.ex: He cut a strip of paper to wrap the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他剪了一条纸来包装礼物。
words.en: To remove a layer from something, or to take off your clothes.

words.tr:
v. 掠夺；抢劫
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
words.ex: The pirates plundered the ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗劫掠了那艘船。
words.en: If someone plunders a place or plunders things from a place, they steal things from it.

words.ex: The pirates depredate the coastal villages.
words.ex_cn: 海盗掠夺沿海村庄。
words.en: To plunder or lay waste to; pillage.

words.ex: The pirates spoliate the ship of its gold.
words.ex_cn: 海盗抢走了船上的黄金。
words.en: To plunder or despoil; to take goods or property by force or without right.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 隐藏

words.ex: He tried to conceal the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图隐藏真相。
words.en: If you conceal something, you prevent it from being seen or known about.

words.tr: adj. 隐秘的；秘密的；隐晦的
words.ex: He gave a cryptic answer and left.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个神秘的回答，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something as cryptic, you mean that it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.ex: He dissembles when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他会假装。
words.en: To dissemble means to conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.

words.ex: He feigns sleep to avoid talking.
words.ex_cn: 他假装睡觉以避免交谈。
words.en: If someone feigns a particular feeling, attitude, or physical condition, they try to make other people think that they have it or are experiencing it, although this is not true.

words.tr:
v. 隐藏；躲藏；
n. 兽皮；
words.ex: He hides the key under the mat.
words.ex_cn: 他把钥匙藏在垫子下面。
words.en: To conceal something or someone from view or discovery.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.ex: He pretends to sleep when his mom asks him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 当妈妈让他打扫房间时，他假装睡觉。
words.en: If you pretend that something is the case, you act in a way that is intended to make people believe that it is the case, although in fact it is not.

words.tr:
n. 屏幕；屏风；掩蔽物；
v. 筛查；掩蔽；
words.ex: The movie is playing on the screen.
words.ex_cn: 电影正在屏幕上播放。
words.en: A screen is a flat surface on which pictures or words are shown, such as the one on a television or computer. It can also refer to a partition used to divide or protect an area. As a verb, to screen means to examine something in order to decide whether it is suitable for a particular purpose, or to protect someone or something from something harmful or unpleasant.

words.tr:
adj. 僻静的；隐僻的； 退隐的
v. 隔离；隔绝；隐居；“seclude”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is secluded in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋坐落在树林中，十分僻静。
words.en: A secluded place is quiet, private, and not near people or things that disturb you.

words.ex: He lives in seclusion in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他住在山里，过着与世隔绝的生活。
words.en: The state of being private and away from other people.

words.ex: The game simulates real traffic conditions.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏模拟了真实的交通状况。
words.en: To simulate is to create a model or representation of a situation, process, or system for the purpose of study, analysis, or training. It involves imitating the conditions of a real event or environment to understand its effects or to practice responses to it.

words.ex: The soldier wore camouflage to hide in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 士兵穿着伪装服在森林中隐藏自己。
words.en: Camouflage is the way in which some animals are colored and shaped so that they cannot easily be seen in their natural surroundings.

words.ex: He wore a scary mask at the Halloween party.
words.ex_cn: 他在万圣节派对上戴了一个可怕的面具。
words.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material that you wear over your face to hide or protect it.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: She wore a white veil on her wedding day.
words.ex_cn: 她在婚礼那天戴了一条白色的面纱。
words.en: A veil is a piece of thin soft cloth that women sometimes wear over their heads and which can also cover their face.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 虚弱

words.ex: The glass is brittle and breaks easily.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃很硬但容易碎。
words.en: If something is brittle, it is hard and easily broken.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: He became emaciated after months of illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病几个月后变得瘦弱不堪。
words.en: To make or become extremely thin, especially as a result of starvation or disease.

words.tr: adj. 瘦弱的；憔悴的； v. “emaciate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The emaciated dog walked slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 那条瘦弱的狗慢慢走在街上。
words.en: Someone who is emaciated is extremely thin and weak because of illness or lack of food.

words.tr: adj. 脆弱的；易碎的；不牢固的；
words.ex: The glass is fragile and might break easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃很脆弱，容易碎。
words.en: If something is fragile, it is easily broken or damaged.

words.ex: The diary entries were fragmentary and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这些日记条目是不完整的，难以理解。
words.en: Consisting of small parts that are disconnected or incomplete.

words.ex: The old man is frail and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人瘦弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: Someone who is frail is not very strong or healthy.

words.tr: n. 无效；虚弱；无能为力；阳萎
words.ex: The new policy showed impotence in solving the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策在解决问题上显得无效。
words.en: The condition of being unable to take effective action; helplessness.

words.tr: adj. 虚弱的；衰弱的；无力的；
words.ex: The old man gave a feeble smile.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人露出虚弱的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as feeble, you mean that they are weak.

words.ex: The family had a meagre meal with just bread and water.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭只吃了一顿贫乏的饭，只有面包和水。
words.en: If you describe an amount or quantity of something as meagre, you are critical of it because it is very small or not enough.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 吸引

words.ex: The sponge absorbs water quickly.
words.ex_cn: 海绵很快吸收水。
words.en: If something absorbs a liquid, gas, or other substance, it soaks it up or takes it in.

words.tr: v. 吸收；“absorb”的现在分词； adj. 吸引人的；
words.ex: The sponge is absorbing water.
words.ex_cn: 海绵正在吸收水。
words.en: If something is absorbing, it is very interesting and holds your attention completely.

words.ex: He is an addict who cannot stop smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他是个无法戒烟的瘾君子。
words.en: An addict is someone who is unable to stop taking harmful drugs, or someone who is very interested in something and spends a lot of time doing it.

words.tr: adj. 上瘾了的；入了迷的
words.ex: He is addicted to video games.
words.ex_cn: 他沉迷于电子游戏。
words.en: If you are addicted to something, you cannot stop doing it or using it, even though it may be harmful to you.

words.ex: She is an attractive woman.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有吸引力的女性。
words.en: An attractive person or thing is pleasing or appealing to look at.

words.tr:
n. 鱼饵；诱惑物
v. 下诱饵
words.ex: He used bread as bait to catch fish.
words.ex_cn: 他用面包当诱饵来钓鱼。
words.en: Bait is something which is used to attract fish or animals so that they can be caught. It can also refer to something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.ex: The cat is catching a mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫正在捉一只老鼠。
words.en: If an illness or a disease is catching, it can be passed from one person to another through touch or through the air. If a mood or an idea is catching, it spreads quickly from one person to another.

words.ex: His charisma made everyone want to follow him.
words.ex_cn: 他的超凡魅力让所有人都想追随他。
words.en: Charisma is a compelling attractiveness or charm that can inspire devotion in others.

words.ex: I draw money from the bank every week.
words.ex_cn: 我每周从银行提取钱。
words.en: To make a picture, pattern, or diagram by making lines and marks, especially with a pen or pencil, on paper.

words.tr: v. 使全神贯注；独占；垄断
words.ex: He is engrossed in reading a novel.
words.ex_cn: 他正全神贯注地读一本小说。
words.en: If something engrosses you, it interests you so much that you do not notice anything else.

words.tr: adj. 全神贯注的； v. “engross”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was engrossed in reading a book.
words.ex_cn: 他全神贯注地看书。
words.en: If you are engrossed in something, you are completely absorbed in it and giving it all your attention.

words.ex: The music enraptured the whole audience.
words.ex_cn: 音乐让整个观众着迷。
words.en: To fill someone with great delight or joy.

words.ex: The shop tries to entice customers with cheap prices.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店试图以低价吸引顾客。
words.en: If you entice someone, you attract them to a particular place or activity by making it seem attractive or interesting.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.tr: adj. 富有魅力的；迷人的；
words.ex: She wore a glamorous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条富有魅力的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as glamorous, you mean that they are more attractive, exciting, or interesting than ordinary people or things.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.tr: v.  使中毒；使醉；使 ...陶醉
words.ex: The dirty water can intoxicate animals.
words.ex_cn: 脏水会使动物中毒。
words.en: To intoxicate someone means to make them lose control of their actions or behavior because they have drunk alcohol or taken drugs. It can also mean to make someone feel very excited and happy.

words.tr: v. 邀请；“invite”的现在分词； adj. 诱人的；吸引人的；
words.ex: He is inviting his friends to dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他正在邀请他的朋友来吃晚饭。
words.en: If you describe something as inviting, you mean that it has good qualities that attract you or make you want to experience it.

words.tr:
v. 吸引；诱惑；引诱
n. 诱惑；诱饵；吸引力
words.ex: The bright colors lure the birds to the feeder.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的颜色吸引鸟类来到喂食器。
words.en: If you lure someone, you tempt them to do something or to go somewhere, especially by offering some form of reward.

words.tr: v. 诱惑；引诱；怂恿；劝诱；
words.ex: The smell of cookies tempted him to eat one.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味诱惑他吃了一块。
words.en: If something tempts you, it makes you want to have it or do it, even though you know you should not.

words.ex: The allure of money made him take the risky job.
words.ex_cn: 金钱的诱惑让他接受了这份高风险的工作。
words.en: The quality of being powerfully and mysteriously attractive or fascinating.

words.ex: The magnet can magnetize the iron nail.
words.ex_cn: 磁铁可以让铁钉磁化。
words.en: To magnetize something means to make it magnetic or to attract it strongly.

words.ex: The movie is fascinating because it shows strange aliens.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极有吸引力，因为它展示了奇怪的外星人。
words.en: If you describe something as fascinating, you find it very interesting and attractive, and your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 战胜

words.ex: He overcame his fear of speaking in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了当众演讲的恐惧。
words.en: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.ex: The subjection of the people to the law is important.
words.ex_cn: 人民对法律的服从很重要。
words.en: The act of subjecting or the state of being subjected, especially to control or authority.

words.ex: He surmounted his fears to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了恐惧，在公众面前发言。
words.en: If you surmount a problem or difficulty, you deal successfully with it.

words.ex: He surpassed his brother in math scores.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学成绩上超过了他弟弟。
words.en: If one person or thing surpasses another, the first is better than, or has more of a particular quality than, the second.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.tr: adj. 止不住的；不能遏制的；不能熄灭的
words.ex: His thirst for knowledge was unquenchable.
words.ex_cn: 他对知识的渴求是止不住的。
words.en: If you describe someone's desire for something as unquenchable, you mean that it is very strong and cannot be satisfied.

words.ex: The hero will vanquish the dragon.
words.ex_cn: 英雄将战胜龙。
words.en: To vanquish someone means to defeat them completely in a battle or a competition.

words.ex: The army conquered the small city after a long battle.
words.ex_cn: 军队经过长期战斗征服了这座小城。
words.en: To conquer means to take control of a country or city and its people by force, or to successfully deal with or control something.

words.tr:
n. 失败；
v. 击败；战胜；
words.ex: The team accepted the defeat with pride.
words.ex_cn: 球队以自豪的态度接受了失败。
words.en: If you defeat someone, you win a victory over them in a battle, game, or contest.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: The king tried to subjugate the rebels.
words.ex_cn: 国王试图征服叛乱者。
words.en: To subjugate a country or group of people means to take complete control of them, especially by defeating them in a war.

words.tr: v. 消灭；歼灭；彻底击败
words.ex: The bomb will annihilate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To annihilate something means to destroy it completely.

words.ex: We took a different route to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们换了条路线以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A route is a way from one place to another, or the path that something follows to reach a destination.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 运动

words.ex: The balloon will ascend into the sky.
words.ex_cn: 气球将升上天空。
words.en: If you ascend a hill or staircase, you go up it. If a staircase or path ascends, it leads up to a higher place.

words.ex: He couldn't budge the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他无法让那个重箱子稍微移动一下。
words.en: If someone will not budge on a matter, or if nothing budges them, they refuse to change their mind or to come to an agreement.

words.ex: The patient is learning to locomote with the aid of a walker.
words.ex_cn: 这位患者正在借助助行器学习移动。
words.en: To move or travel from one place to another.

words.ex: The motion of the ball is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 球的运动非常快。
words.en: The action or process of moving or being moved.

words.ex: The cat likes to roam around the garden.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫喜欢在花园里游荡。
words.en: To roam means to move about or travel without any definite purpose or destination.

words.tr:
n. 隆隆声；辘辘声
v. 隆隆作响；辘辘行驶
words.ex: The dog let out a low rumble.
words.ex_cn: 狗发出了一声低沉的咆哮。
words.en: To make a continuous deep, resonant sound; to speak in a low, deep voice.

words.tr:
n. 规模；等级；比例（尺）；刻度；秤；
v. 改变…大小；
words.ex: The scale of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的规模让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A scale is a set of levels or numbers which are used in a particular system of measuring things or are used when comparing things.

words.tr:
n. 茎；柄；梗
v. 跟踪；偷偷接近；昂首阔步地走
words.ex: The stalk of the sunflower is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 向日葵的茎很高。
words.en: The main stem of a plant, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean. Also, to pursue or approach stealthily.

words.ex: The stray dog wandered into the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 这只走失的狗走进了后院。
words.en: If someone or something strays, they wander away from where they are supposed to be.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
n. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
words.ex: They stroll in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们晚饭后在公园里闲逛。
words.en: If you stroll somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 遗留

words.ex: He left his books as a bequest to the library.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的书作为遗赠给了图书馆。
words.en: A bequest is money or property which you legally leave to someone when you die.

words.ex: Heredity determines eye color in humans.
words.ex_cn: 遗传决定人类的眼睛颜色。
words.en: Heredity is the process by which features and characteristics are passed on from parents to their children before the children are born.

words.ex: His legacy includes many charity schools.
words.ex_cn: 他的遗产包括许多慈善学校。
words.en: Something handed down from an ancestor or a predecessor or from the past.

words.ex: The old temple is a relic from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙是来自古代的遗迹。
words.en: An object surviving from an earlier time, especially one of historical or sentimental interest.

words.tr:
v. 剩下；留下；依然不变；
n. 遗迹；残余；遗体；
words.ex: Only two cookies remains on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌上只剩下两块饼干了。
words.en: The parts left over after other parts have been removed, used, or destroyed.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 学习

words.tr:
adj. 学术的；
n. 大学教师；学者；
words.ex: He published an academic paper on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于气候变化的学术论文。
words.en: relating to education, especially at college or university level

words.ex: The class will commence at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程将在上午9点开始。
words.en: To begin something; to start.

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.tr:
n. 信用；赊账；赞扬；贷款；荣誉；
v. 相信；
words.ex: He has good credit with the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他在银行有良好的信用。
words.en: If you are allowed credit, you are allowed to pay for goods or services several weeks or months after you have received them.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.ex: His discourse on climate change was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他关于气候变化的论述清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: Discourse is spoken or written communication between people, especially serious discussion of a particular subject.

words.ex: His ken does not include quantum physics.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识范围不包括量子物理。
words.en: Ken is the range of one's knowledge or understanding.

words.ex: He is literate and can read simple books.
words.ex_cn: 他有读写能力，能读简单的书。
words.en: A literate person is able to read and write, and has a good education.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.ex: He handed me a pamphlet about the new park.
words.ex_cn: 他递给我一份关于新公园的小册子。
words.en: A pamphlet is a small book containing information on a particular subject or expressing political or religious views.

words.ex: He bought new stationery for school.
words.ex_cn: 他为学校买了新的文具。
words.en: Stationery refers to the materials used for writing, such as paper, pens, and envelopes.

words.ex: His thesis is that exercise improves memory.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是锻炼能改善记忆力。
words.en: A thesis is a long piece of writing based on your own ideas and research that you do as part of a university degree, especially a higher degree such as a PhD.

words.ex: I asked the school for a transcript of my grades.
words.ex_cn: 我向学校要了一份成绩单的副本。
words.en: A transcript is a written or printed version of something that has been recorded or spoken, especially in the context of academic records.

words.ex: He wrote an essay about his summer trip.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于他暑假旅行的文章。
words.en: An essay is a short piece of writing on a particular subject.

words.ex: He wrote his dissertation on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的学位论文。
words.en: A dissertation is a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 举止

words.ex: The government took quick action to fix the problem.
words.ex_cn: 政府迅速采取行动解决问题。
words.en: The fact or process of doing something, typically to achieve an aim.

words.ex: The child behaves well in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在课堂上表现得很好。
words.en: To behave means to act in a particular way, especially in a way that is good or correct.

words.ex: His behaviour at school is very good.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校的行为很好。
words.en: The way in which one acts or conducts oneself, especially towards others.

words.tr:
v. 实施；传导（电、热）；
n. 行为；举止；
words.ex: The company will conduct a survey next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司将在下周进行一项调查。
words.en: To organize and carry out a particular activity.

words.ex: He works in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售部工作。
words.en: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university.

words.ex: He spoke in a polite manner.
words.ex_cn: 他以礼貌的方式说话。
words.en: The way in which something is done or happens.

words.ex: His calm demeanour surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他冷静的举止让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Demeanour refers to the way in which a person behaves towards others; their outward behaviour or bearing.

words.ex: He sat with good posture at the desk.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在书桌前，姿势端正。
words.en: Your posture is the way in which you hold your body when you are standing or sitting.

words.ex: The king rode in a wooden carriage drawn by four horses.
words.ex_cn: 国王乘坐一辆由四匹马拉的木制四轮马车。
words.en: A carriage is a vehicle with four wheels that is pulled by horses and is used for carrying people.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 束缚

words.ex: He felt trapped in bondage.
words.ex_cn: 他感到被困在束缚中。
words.en: Bondage refers to the state of being a slave or being under the control of another person.

words.tr: adj. 一定会；密切相关的；有义务的； v. “bind”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is bound to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他一定会赢得比赛。
words.en: If one person, thing, or situation is bound to another, they are closely connected with each other, and it is difficult for them to be separated or to escape from each other. If you say that something is bound to happen, you mean that you are sure it will happen, because it is a natural consequence of something that is already known or exists.

words.tr:
v. 检查；核对；
n. 检查；支票；阻止；
words.ex: Please check your homework before class.
words.ex_cn: 请在上课前检查你的作业。
words.en: To examine something in order to determine its accuracy, quality, or condition, or to make sure that something is correct or safe.

words.ex: The law circumscribes what companies can do.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制了公司能做的事情。
words.en: To circumscribe something means to limit its size, activity, or scope, often by setting boundaries or restrictions.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.ex: The heavy fine is a deterrent to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 高额罚款是一种威慑作弊的力量。
words.en: Something that discourages or is intended to discourage someone from doing something.

words.tr:
v. 为 ... 上脚镣；束缚；限制
n. 脚镣；桎梏；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner was fettered with chains.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯被锁链束缚着。
words.en: A fetter is a chain or shackle for the feet, or something that confines or restrains.

words.tr: n. 牵狗的链子或皮带；控制；约束
words.ex: He holds the dog's leash tightly.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧握着狗的牵引绳。
words.en: A leash is a rope or a strap that you attach to a dog's collar so that you can control the dog.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.tr:
n. 手铐；脚镣；镣铐；束缚物
v. 给...戴上镣铐；束缚
words.ex: The prisoner wore iron shackle on his ankle.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯脚上戴着铁镣。
words.en: A shackle is a pair of metal rings connected by a chain which are fastened around someone's wrists or ankles in order to prevent them from moving or escaping.

words.ex: He practices temperance by drinking little alcohol.
words.ex_cn: 他通过少喝酒来节制。
words.en: Temperance is the practice of moderation or self-restraint, especially in the consumption of alcohol.

words.tr:
n. 马梏；量规；束缚物；渔网
v. 束缚；妨碍；用网捕捉
words.ex: The horse wore a trammel to control its legs.
words.ex_cn: 这匹马戴着马梏来控制它的腿。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is trammeled, you mean that their freedom of action or movement is restricted.

words.ex: He was imprisoned for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窃而被监禁。
words.en: To put someone in prison or keep them as a prisoner.

words.ex: The rule is limitative and allows only two tries.
words.ex_cn: 这个规则是限制性的，只允许尝试两次。
words.en: Imposing restrictions or limitations.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 秉性

words.tr: adj. 习惯的；惯常的； v. “accustom”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is accustomed to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯早起。
words.en: If you are accustomed to something, you know it so well or have experienced it so often that it seems natural, unsurprising, or easy to deal with.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.tr: adj. 弯曲的； v. 弯曲；使弯曲；“bend”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The bent pipe leaked water.
words.ex_cn: 弯曲的管道漏水了。
words.en: Bent is used to describe something that is not straight but has a curve or angle in it. It can also refer to someone's natural talent or inclination towards a particular activity or subject.

words.ex: He habitually wakes up at 6 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯每天早上六点起床。
words.en: If someone does something habitually, they do it regularly or as a habit.

words.tr: adj. 倾向于…的； v. “incline”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is inclined to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他倾向于帮助别人。
words.en: Having a tendency or preference towards something; likely to do or be something.

words.ex: He inured himself to the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 他让自己适应了寒冷的天气。
words.en: If you are inured to something unpleasant, you have become used to it so that it no longer affects you.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.ex: He is prone to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If you are prone to a particular problem or characteristic, you are likely to be affected by it or to have it.

words.ex: He has a propensity for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他有说实话的倾向。
words.en: A propensity is a natural tendency to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: Children tend to be more active in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 孩子往往在早上更活跃。
words.en: If someone tends to do something, they usually do it or they often do it.

words.ex: He has a talent for playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他有弹钢琴的才能。
words.en: If someone has a talent for something, they have a natural ability to do it well.

words.ex: He has an inclination to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他有帮助他人的倾向。
words.en: An inclination is a feeling that makes you want to act in a particular way, or a tendency to do something.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.ex: He showed partiality toward his favorite student.
words.ex_cn: 他对最喜欢的学生表现出偏袒。
words.en: If you have a partiality for something, you like it very much.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 拖延

words.ex: The meeting will adjourn at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 会议将在下午5点休会。
words.en: If a meeting or trial is adjourned, or if it adjourns, it is stopped for a short time.

words.ex: He will defer his trip until next month.
words.ex_cn: 他将把旅行推迟到下个月。
words.en: If you defer an event or action, you arrange for it to happen at a later date, rather than immediately or at the previously planned time.

words.tr:
n. 推迟；延缓；耽搁；
v. 推迟；延缓；耽搁；
words.ex: The flight had a delay because of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 由于风暴，航班推迟了。
words.en: If you delay doing something, you do not do it immediately or at the planned or expected time, but you leave it until later.

words.ex: The police will detain the suspect for questioning.
words.ex_cn: 警察将扣留嫌疑人进行审问。
words.en: If someone is detained, they are officially held in a place, especially a prison, and are not allowed to leave.

words.ex: They decided to postpone the meeting until next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定把会议推迟到下周。
words.en: To postpone something means to arrange for it to take place at a later time than was originally planned.

words.ex: They decided to prolong the meeting by one hour.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定将会议延长一小时。
words.en: To prolong something means to make it last longer.

words.ex: He tries to protract the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他试图延长会议。
words.en: To protract something means to make it last longer than usual or necessary, often in a way that is annoying or inconvenient.

words.ex: The rain will retard the construction of the road.
words.ex_cn: 雨水会延迟道路的建设。
words.en: To retard something means to delay it or make it happen more slowly than it would otherwise.

words.tr: adj. 迟的；缓慢的；迟缓的
words.ex: He is tardy for school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上学都迟到。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tardy, you think that they are later than they should be or later than expected.

words.ex: He kept putting off his homework because of procrastination.
words.ex_cn: 他因为拖延一直推迟做作业。
words.en: Procrastination is the action of delaying or postponing something.

words.tr: v. 暂停；中止；延期； suspending
words.ex: The school will suspend the class due to snow.
words.ex_cn: 由于下雪，学校将暂停课程。
words.en: If you suspend something, you delay it or stop it from happening for a while or until a decision is made about it.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 探索

words.ex: They explore the forest to find hidden caves.
words.ex_cn: 他们探索森林以寻找隐藏的洞穴。
words.en: To explore means to travel over or through an unfamiliar area in order to learn about it or to search for something valuable.

words.tr:
n. 白鼬；雪貂
v. 用雪貂打猎；搜寻
words.ex: The ferret ran under the fence.
words.ex_cn: 白鼬从篱笆下跑过去了。
words.en: A ferret is a small, fierce animal which is used for hunting rabbits and rats. To ferret means to search for something persistently.

words.ex: He gropped in the dark for the light switch.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中摸索着找电灯开关。
words.en: If you grope for something that you cannot see, you try to find it by moving your hands around in order to feel it.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.tr:
n. 风险；
v. 冒...的危险；
words.ex: He took a risk by starting his own business.
words.ex_cn: 他创业时承担了风险。
words.en: If there is a risk of something unpleasant, there is a possibility that it will happen.

words.ex: He seeks help when he is stuck.
words.ex_cn: 当他遇到困难时，他会寻求帮助。
words.en: If you seek something, you try to find it or obtain it.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.tr:
v. 搜寻；翻找；乱翻
n. 翻箱倒柜的寻找
words.ex: He rummaged through his drawer to find the keys.
words.ex_cn: 他翻找抽屉找钥匙。
words.en: If you rummage through something, you search for something you want by moving things around in a careless or hurried way.

words.tr:
v. 乱摸；摸索；笨手笨脚地做
n. 摸索；笨手笨脚
words.ex: He fumbled for his keys in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他在黑暗中乱摸着找钥匙。
words.en: If you fumble with something, you try to hold, move, or find it with your hands in a clumsy way.

words.ex: The police will investigate the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方将调查这起事故。
words.en: If someone, especially an official, investigates an event, situation, or claim, they try to find out what happened or what is the truth.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 失误

words.tr: adj. 失败的；夭折的；发育不完全的
words.ex: The abortive plan failed before it started.
words.ex_cn: 这个失败的计划在开始前就失败了。
words.en: Failing to produce the intended result; unsuccessful.

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；失误
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；失误；跌跌撞撞地走
words.ex: He made a big blunder in the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中犯了一个大错误。
words.en: A blunder is a stupid or careless mistake.

words.ex: He is credulous and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很轻信，相信他听到的每一个故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as credulous, you have a low opinion of them because they are too ready to believe what people tell them and are easily deceived.

words.tr: adj. 有缺点的；有缺陷的；有毛病的；
words.ex: The defective phone wouldn't turn on.
words.ex_cn: 这部有缺点的手机无法开机。
words.en: If something is defective, there is something wrong with it and it does not work properly.

words.ex: The defect in the phone made it hard to use.
words.ex_cn: 手机的缺陷让它很难使用。
words.en: A defect is a fault or imperfection in a person or thing.

words.ex: The drawback of this phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的缺点是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A drawback is a feature of something that makes it less useful or desirable than it could be.

words.ex: He made an error in his math homework.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学作业中犯了一个错误。
words.en: An error is a mistake.

words.ex: His answer was erroneous because he added wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案是错误的，因为他加错了。
words.en: If you describe someone's beliefs or opinions as erroneous, you mean that they are incorrect and based on false information.

words.ex: Everyone is fallible, even teachers.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都会犯错，即使是老师。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is fallible, you mean that they are not perfect and are likely to make mistakes or to fail in what they are doing.

words.ex: The flaw in the glass made it break easily.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃上的瑕疵让它很容易碎。
words.en: A flaw is a mistake or weakness in something that makes it less effective or valuable.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.tr: adj. 不留心的；不注意的
words.ex: He was heedless of the warning signs.
words.ex_cn: 他对警告信号毫不在意。
words.en: If you are heedless of someone or something, you do not take any notice of them.

words.ex: He ignored the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 他忽视了警告标志。
words.en: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

words.tr: adj. 天真无邪的；无辜的；
words.ex: The innocent child smiled at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 那个天真无邪的孩子对陌生人笑了。
words.en: If someone is innocent, they did not commit a crime which they have been accused of.

words.ex: His neglect of the project caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 他对项目的疏忽导致了延误。
words.en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the attention or care that they need.

words.ex: His negligence caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: Negligence is failure to take proper care over something that you are responsible for, which might cause damage or loss.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；粗心的；不在意的
words.ex: He was negligent in doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他做作业时很疏忽。
words.en: If you say that someone is negligent, you mean that they do not take enough care over something that they are responsible for.

words.ex: He fell into oblivion after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后，他被遗忘了。
words.en: A state of being forgotten or unknown.

words.tr:
adj. 即时的；未经准备的；唐突无礼的
adv. 即时地；未经思索地；随便地
words.ex: He gave an offhand answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个即时的回答。
words.en: If you say something offhand, you say it without checking the details or facts of it beforehand.

words.ex: He omitted the last word in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他省略了句子中的最后一个词。
words.en: If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.

words.ex: He overlooked the mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了报告中的错误。
words.en: If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.

words.ex: He went outside regardless of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾下雨就出去了。
words.en: If you say that someone does something regardless, you mean that they do it without taking account of the possible problems or difficulties.

words.ex: It's ridiculous to think he can run a mile in one minute.
words.ex_cn: 认为他能在一分钟内跑完一英里是荒谬的。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is ridiculous, you mean that they are very foolish.

words.tr: adj. 不修边幅的；邋遢的
words.ex: He wore slovenly clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着邋遢的衣服去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as slovenly, you disapprove of them because they are careless and untidy in their appearance or habits.

words.ex: This broken phone is useless.
words.ex_cn: 这部坏掉的手机毫无用处。
words.en: If something is useless, it is not able to do what it is supposed to do or is not effective.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 认可

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He finally admit his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true.

words.ex: He affirm that the plan will work.
words.ex_cn: 他断言这个计划会成功。
words.en: If you affirm that something is true or that something exists, you state firmly and publicly that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr: v. 批准；认可；通过；赞成(连of)
words.ex: My mom will approve my new phone.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈会同意我买新手机。
words.en: If you approve of an action, event, or suggestion, you like it or are pleased about it.

words.tr: v. 承认；公开宣称声明
words.ex: He avows his love for her.
words.ex_cn: 他坦承自己对她的爱。
words.en: If you avow something, you declare it or admit it openly.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: He bought a concession ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了电影的减价票。
words.en: A concession is a point or principle that is granted or acknowledged in the course of an argument or negotiation, often as a compromise or to facilitate agreement.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.ex: He confesses that he made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承认自己犯了一个错误。
words.en: If you confess to doing something, you admit that you did it.

words.ex: The teacher showed connivance when students cheated.
words.ex_cn: 当学生作弊时，老师表现出默许。
words.en: Connivance is the act of conniving, especially by pretending not to notice something bad that is happening.

words.ex: The teacher connived at the students' cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师纵容了学生的作弊行为。
words.en: If one person connives with another to do something wrong, they secretly allow or help them to do it.

words.ex: The witness corroborated his story with photos.
words.ex_cn: 证人用照片证实了他的说法。
words.en: To corroborate something that has been said or reported means to provide evidence or information that supports it.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.tr:
n. 补助金；授予物；
v. 承认；授予；允许；
words.ex: The university received a grant for scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一笔用于科学研究的补助金。
words.en: If someone in authority grants you something, or if something is granted to you, you are allowed to have it or do it.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.tr:
v. 原谅；宽恕；请再说一遍
n. 原谅；宽恕
words.ex: Can you pardon me for being late?
words.ex_cn: 你能原谅我迟到吗？
words.en: If you pardon someone, you forgive them for something they have done wrong. If someone is pardoned, they are officially forgiven for a crime they have committed.

words.tr: adj. 可容许的；可承认的
words.ex: It is permissible to use a calculator in this test.
words.ex_cn: 在这次考试中使用计算器是允许的。
words.en: If something is permissible, it is considered to be acceptable because it does not break any laws or rules.

words.tr: adj. 放任的；纵容的；许可的
words.ex: Her parents are permissive and let her stay out late.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母很宽容，让她很晚才回家。
words.en: A permissive person, society, or system allows people a lot of freedom to do what they want.

words.tr:
n. 许可证；
v. 允许；准许；
words.ex: He showed his fishing permit to the officer.
words.ex_cn: 他向官员出示了他的钓鱼许可证。
words.en: If someone permits something, they allow it to happen. If they permit you to do something, they allow you to do it.

words.ex: The Senate will ratify the treaty next week.
words.ex_cn: 参议院下周将批准这项条约。
words.en: If a country or organization ratifies a treaty or agreement, they make it official by giving their formal approval to it, usually by signing it or voting for it.

words.ex: The reception at the hotel was very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的接待非常友好。
words.en: The act of receiving or being received, especially in a formal or official context.

words.tr: n. 认可；识别；认识；承认；
words.ex: His hard work got recognition from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力得到了老板的认可。
words.en: The action or process of recognizing or being recognized, in particular.

words.ex: I recognize her face from school.
words.ex_cn: 我从学校认出了她的脸。
words.en: If you recognize someone or something, you know who or what they are because you have seen or heard them before.

words.tr: adj. 心照不宣的；不作声的
words.ex: They have a tacit understanding about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们对规则有一种心照不宣的理解。
words.en: If you refer to someone's tacit agreement or approval, you mean they are agreeing to something or approving it without actually saying so, often because they are unwilling to admit to doing so.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 忍受

words.ex: You must abide by the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: If you can't abide someone or something, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: The noise from the party is insufferable.
words.ex_cn: 派对的噪音令人无法忍受。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as insufferable, you are emphasizing that they are very unpleasant or annoying.

words.tr:
v. 站立；忍受；
n. 立足点；
words.ex: The boy stands near the door.
words.ex_cn: 男孩站在门附近。
words.en: If you stand somewhere, you are in an upright position with your feet on the ground. If something stands somewhere, it is in an upright position in that place.

words.ex: The weather was tolerable, so we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天气还可以忍受，所以我们去散步了。
words.en: If something is tolerable, it is acceptable or bearable, even though it is not very good or pleasant.

words.ex: I can't tolerate loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 我无法容忍巨大的噪音。
words.en: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

words.ex: He had to undergo surgery last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周不得不接受手术。
words.en: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you or is done to you.

words.ex: He ate too much and his stomach hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多了，胃疼。
words.en: The stomach is the organ in your body where food is digested after you have eaten it.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 勤奋

words.ex: He is an assiduous student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤奋的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is assiduous works hard or does things very thoroughly.

words.tr:
n. 企图；试图；
v. 企图；试图；
words.ex: His attempt to cheat on the test failed.
words.ex_cn: 他企图在考试中作弊，但失败了。
words.en: To make an effort to achieve or complete something, especially something difficult.

words.ex: He is diligent in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都很勤奋地做作业。
words.en: Someone who is diligent works hard and is careful and thorough.

words.tr:
n. 尽力；尝试；
v. 尽力；奋力；
words.ex: His endeavor to finish the project took all his energy.
words.ex_cn: 他为完成这个项目付出了全部努力。
words.en: An endeavor is an attempt to do something, especially something new or original.

words.ex: He is an industrious student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤勉的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is industrious works hard and is determined.

words.ex: Cleaning the whole house is a laborious task.
words.ex_cn: 打扫整个房子是一项耗时费力的任务。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as laborious, you mean that it takes a lot of time and effort.

words.ex: He is a studious student who always does his homework carefully.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个认真学习的学生，总是认真完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is studious spends a lot of time studying and reading.

words.ex: He made a painstaking effort to fix the small details.
words.ex_cn: 他细心地努力修正每一个小细节。
words.en: If you describe someone's work as painstaking, you mean that they do it very carefully and thoroughly, often taking a long time.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 强迫

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.ex: The law compels drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律强迫司机系安全带。
words.en: If a situation, a rule, or a person compels you to do something, they force you to do it.

words.tr: adj. 无法控制行为的；禁不住的；
words.ex: He has a compulsive habit of checking the door lock.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种无法控制地检查门锁的习惯。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as compulsive, you mean that they cannot stop themselves doing or wanting something, even though it may be harmful or unreasonable.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.tr:
n. 压力；压强；
v. 对…施加压力；
words.ex: He feels pressure from his parents to get good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到来自父母要取得好成绩的压力。
words.en: Pressure is the force that you produce when you press hard on something, or the force that is produced by a particular amount of gas or liquid in a confined space.

words.ex: They tease him because he wears funny hats.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他戴滑稽的帽子而戏弄他。
words.en: To tease someone means to make fun of them or try to provoke them in a playful way.

words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.tr: v. 强使接受；打扰；闯入
words.ex: He tried to obtrude his opinions on the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图强使组里接受他的观点。
words.en: To force something on someone in a way that is unwelcome or intrusive.

words.ex: The coach used coercive methods to make players train harder.
words.ex_cn: 教练使用了强制性手段让球员更努力地训练。
words.en: Coercive actions or powers are used to force people to do things that they are unwilling to do.

words.ex: The danger impels him to act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 危险驱使他迅速行动。
words.en: If something impels you to do something, it makes you feel very strongly that you must do it.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 破坏

words.tr:
n. 违背；
v. 攻破；
words.ex: The company committed a breach of contract.
words.ex_cn: 该公司违反了合同。
words.en: A breach of a law, rule, or agreement is an act of breaking it.

words.tr: n. 崩溃；故障；细目分类；
words.ex: The stress led to a breakdown.
words.ex_cn: 压力导致了崩溃。
words.en: A breakdown is a failure of a system, machine, or relationship, or a sudden collapse in someone's mental health.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr:
n. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
v. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
words.ex: The car crash happened at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 汽车碰撞发生在十字路口。
words.en: If a vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed.

words.ex: He crumpled the paper in his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他把纸揉皱了。
words.en: If you crumple something such as paper or cloth, or if it crumples, it is squashed and becomes full of untidy creases and folds.

words.ex: He crushed the can with his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他用手把罐子压碎了。
words.en: To crush something means to press it very hard so that its shape is destroyed or so that it breaks into pieces. It can also mean to defeat someone completely, or to make someone feel extremely upset or disappointed.

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
words.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely. It can also mean to defeat someone completely in a discussion, argument, or competition.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.ex: The earthquake caused total devastation in the city.
words.ex_cn: 地震给这座城市造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: The state of being devastated; severe and widespread destruction or damage.

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

words.tr: v. 损毁…的外形；使变丑
words.ex: The accident disfigured his face.
words.ex_cn: 那次事故使他的脸变形了。
words.en: To disfigure someone or something means to spoil their appearance.

words.ex: The old bridge began disintegration after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥在风暴后开始崩解。
words.en: The process of breaking into small parts or pieces and losing strength or effectiveness.

words.ex: The storm disrupted the train service.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴中断了火车服务。
words.en: To disrupt a system, process, or event means to prevent it from continuing or operating in a normal way.

words.ex: The fire engulfed the old house.
words.ex_cn: 大火吞噬了那座老房子。
words.en: If one thing engulfs another, it completely covers or hides it, often in a sudden and unexpected way.

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.ex: The glass broke into small fragments.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃碎成了小碎片。
words.en: A fragment of something is a small piece or part of it.

words.ex: The slow internet frustrates me.
words.ex_cn: 慢速的网络让我感到沮丧。
words.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to deal with the problems it creates.

words.ex: She put the wet clothes into the mangle to remove the water.
words.ex_cn: 她把湿衣服放进衣物轧干机里去除水分。
words.en: To mangle something means to severely damage it, usually by twisting, tearing, or cutting it, so that it is no longer in its original condition.

words.tr:
v. 毁坏；破坏；劫掠
n. 破坏；蹂躏
words.ex: The storm ravaged the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个小村庄。
words.en: To ravage means to cause severe and extensive damage to something.

words.tr: v. 使夷为平地；彻底摧毁
words.ex: They will raze the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周将把那座旧建筑夷为平地。
words.en: To raze a building, town, or forest means to completely destroy it, especially by knocking it down or burning it.

words.ex: The rupture in the pipe caused a flood.
words.ex_cn: 管道的破裂导致了洪水。
words.en: A rupture is a severe injury in which an internal part of your body tears or bursts open, or the act of breaking or bursting something.

words.tr:
n. 小块；碎片；废金属；吵架
v. 废弃；取消
adj. 废弃的
words.ex: He picked up a scrap of paper from the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他从地上捡起一张纸片。
words.en: A scrap is a small piece or amount of something, especially one that is left over after the greater part has been used. It can also mean to discard or get rid of something as being no longer useful or necessary.

words.tr: v. 使粉碎；使破碎；使破灭；
words.ex: The stone shattered when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 石头撞到地面时碎裂了。
words.en: If something shatters or is shattered, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.ex: He smashed the glass with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把玻璃打碎了。
words.en: To break something into pieces violently and noisily, or to cause something to do this by dropping, throwing, or hitting it.

words.ex: Parents often spoil their children with too many toys.
words.ex_cn: 父母经常用太多玩具宠坏孩子。
words.en: To spoil something means to reduce its quality or value, often by damaging it in some way. It can also mean to treat someone, especially a child, with too much kindness or indulgence, leading to their detriment.

words.tr:
n. 球类运动（squash）；
v. 压碎；
words.ex: He plays squash every weekend with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他每周末和朋友打壁球。
words.en: To squash something means to press or squeeze it so that it becomes flat, soft, or out of shape. It can also refer to the sport of squash or a type of vegetable.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 叛变

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.ex: His defection shocked the whole team.
words.ex_cn: 他的叛逃让整个团队震惊。
words.en: The act of abandoning a cause, party, or nation, especially in favor of an opposing one.

words.tr:
v. 推翻；颠覆；打倒
n. 推翻；颠覆；打倒
words.ex: The court will overturn the old law.
words.ex_cn: 法院将推翻这项旧法律。
words.en: If a decision, result, etc. is overturned, it is officially changed so that it becomes the opposite of what it was before.

words.tr:
n. 情节；小块用地；
v. 绘图；
words.ex: The plot of the movie was very exciting.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的情节非常精彩。
words.en: A plot is a secret plan by a group of people to do something that is illegal or wrong, especially against a person or a government. It can also refer to the main events of a play, novel, movie, or similar work, devised and presented by the writer as an interrelated sequence. Additionally, a plot can be a small piece of land that is used or intended for a specific purpose.

words.ex: The rebel fought against the king's rules.
words.ex_cn: 这位叛逆者反抗国王的法令。
words.en: A rebel is a person who opposes or fights against people in authority.

words.ex: The rebellion against the king failed.
words.ex_cn: 反对国王的叛乱失败了。
words.en: A rebellion is an organized attempt to overthrow a government or authority by a group of people.

words.ex: The riot broke out after the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
words.en: A riot is a violent disturbance of the peace by a crowd.

words.ex: They tried to subvert the government.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图颠覆政府。
words.en: To subvert means to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution.

words.ex: He was punished for treason against the king.
words.ex_cn: 他因对国王叛国而受到惩罚。
words.en: Treason is the crime of betraying your country, for example by helping its enemies or by trying to remove its government using violence.

words.tr: adj. 狂暴的；骚动的；动荡的；汹涌的
words.ex: The turbulent sea made the boat shake.
words.ex_cn: 汹涌的海让船摇晃。
words.en: A turbulent situation, time, or relationship is one in which there is a lot of change, confusion, and often conflict.

words.tr: n. 混乱；动荡；骚乱；恐慌
words.ex: The storm caused turmoil in the town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty.

words.ex: The people started an uprising against the unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 人们因不公平的规则而发动了起义。
words.en: An uprising is a violent act of opposition by many people in one area against those who are in power there.

words.ex: The announcement caused an uproar in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这个公告在小镇上引起了轩然大波。
words.en: A loud and impassioned noise or disturbance.

words.ex: The people tried to overthrow the corrupt government.
words.ex_cn: 人民试图推翻腐败的政府。
words.en: To overthrow a government or a leader means to remove them from power, often by force.

words.tr: n. 叛徒；背叛者；卖国贼
words.ex: He was called a traitor for helping the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为帮助敌人而被称为叛徒。
words.en: A traitor is a person who betrays a friend, country, principle, etc.

words.tr: n. 暴动；起义；造反；叛乱
words.ex: The insurgence broke out after the election.
words.ex_cn: 选举后爆发了暴动。
words.en: An insurgence is a violent uprising against an authority or government.

words.tr:
v. 叛乱；反叛；（使）厌恶
n. 叛乱；厌恶；反感
words.ex: The people revolt against the unfair rules.
words.ex_cn: 人们反抗不公平的规则。
words.en: If a large number of people revolt, they refuse to be controlled or ruled, and take action against authority, often violent action.

words.ex: The storm caused an upheaval in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A very large change in something that often causes confusion or problems.

words.ex: The king suffered from treachery by his own friend.
words.ex_cn: 国王被自己朋友背叛了。
words.en: Treachery is behavior that involves betraying someone's trust or being disloyal.

words.tr: n. 大破坏；大毁坏；大混乱；
words.ex: The storm caused havoc in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给这个小镇带来了大破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as havoc, you mean that it causes a great deal of disorder, confusion, or destruction.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 判断

words.ex: He affirm that the plan will work.
words.ex_cn: 他断言这个计划会成功。
words.en: If you affirm that something is true or that something exists, you state firmly and publicly that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr: v. 断言；宣称；坚持；维护
words.ex: He asserts that the answer is correct.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持认为答案是正确的。
words.en: To state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.

words.ex: He concluded that the experiment failed.
words.ex_cn: 他得出结论说实验失败了。
words.en: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

words.ex: They deem this plan too risky.
words.ex_cn: 他们认为这个计划太冒险了。
words.en: If you deem something to be the case, you consider that it is the case.

words.ex: The teacher will determine the winner of the contest.
words.ex_cn: 老师将确定比赛的获胜者。
words.en: If you determine something, you decide it or settle it.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.ex: The teacher gave students discretion to choose their own topic.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了学生自行选择题目的权利。
words.en: Discretion is the quality of behaving in a quiet and controlled way without drawing attention to yourself or giving away personal or private information.

words.tr: adj. 教条的；武断的；固执己见的
words.ex: He is dogmatic about his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己信念非常固执。
words.en: If you say that someone is dogmatic, you are critical of them because they are convinced that they are right, and refuse to consider that other opinions might also be justified.

words.ex: His handwriting is illegible.
words.ex_cn: 他的字迹无法辨认。
