words.en: If something is illegible, it is impossible to read because the letters or characters are not clear, are not formed properly, or are obscured in some way.

words.tr:
adj. 待定的；即将发生的
prep. 在等待…期间；直到…为止
words.ex: The decision is pending.
words.ex_cn: 决定尚未做出。
words.en: If something is pending, it has not yet happened or been decided, and is often waiting for something else to happen first.

words.ex: He resolved the problem with a simple plan.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个简单的计划解决了问题。
words.en: If you resolve to do something, you make a firm decision to do it.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 迷惑

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使...不知所措
words.ex: The strange signs bewilder the children.
words.ex_cn: 这些奇怪的符号让孩子们感到迷惑。
words.en: If something bewilders you, it is so confusing or difficult that you cannot understand it.

words.tr:
v. 使模糊；使看不清；弄污
n. 模糊
words.ex: The rain made the lights blur.
words.ex_cn: 雨使灯光变得模糊。
words.en: If something blurs your vision, it makes you unable to see things clearly.

words.ex: The magic show captivates the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If you are captivated by someone or something, you find them fascinating and attractive.

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.tr:
v. 使目眩；使眼花；使惊叹
n. 耀眼；眩惑；灿烂
words.ex: The stars dazzle at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的星星闪耀夺目。
words.en: If something dazzles you, it is so bright that you cannot see properly for a short time. It can also mean to greatly impress someone.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.ex: The old man gave an enigmatic smile.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人露出了一个神秘的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as enigmatic, you mean they are mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.ex: The cat got entangled in the string.
words.ex_cn: 猫被绳子缠住了。
words.en: If something is entangled in something else, it is caught or twisted around it, or mixed with it so that it is difficult to separate the two things.

words.ex: The magic show enthralls the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们着迷。
words.en: If you are enthralled by something, you are so interested and excited by it that you give it all your attention.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊其词的；难以解释的
words.ex: His answer was equivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可。
words.en: If you are equivocal, you are deliberately vague in what you say, because you want to avoid speaking the truth or making a decision.

words.tr: v. 强烈吸引住；使着迷；
words.ex: The magic show fascinated the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演深深吸引了孩子们。
words.en: If something fascinates you, it interests and delights you so much that your thoughts tend to concentrate on it.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；错综复杂的曲径；
words.ex: The children got lost in the maze.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A maze is a complex system of paths or passages in which it is easy to get lost.

words.ex: The riddle perplexed the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜语让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something perplexes you, it confuses and worries you because you do not understand it or because it causes you difficulty.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.tr:
v. （使）纠缠；使陷入；使混乱
n. 纠缠；混乱；纠纷
words.ex: The cat got into a tangle with the yarn.
words.ex_cn: 猫和毛线缠在一起了。
words.en: If something is tangled or tangles, it becomes twisted together in an untidy way.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.ex: He deluded himself into thinking he would win.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗自己，以为自己会赢。
words.en: If you delude yourself, you let yourself believe that something is true, even though it is not true.

words.ex: The witch bewitches the prince with her song.
words.ex_cn: 女巫用她的歌声迷住了王子。
words.en: To bewitch someone means to attract them so strongly that they seem to be under a spell.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.tr: v. 施催眠术；使（某人）着迷
words.ex: The man tries to hypnotize the crowd with his watch.
words.ex_cn: 这个人试图用他的手表催眠人群。
words.en: To hypnotize someone means to put them into a state of hypnosis.

chapters.name: Word List 34 行为 肯定

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.ex: He affirm that the plan will work.
words.ex_cn: 他断言这个计划会成功。
words.en: If you affirm that something is true or that something exists, you state firmly and publicly that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He gave a definite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了肯定的答案。
words.en: If something is definite, it is firm and clear, and unlikely to be changed.

words.ex: The test results confirm he has the disease.
words.ex_cn: 检测结果证实他患有这种疾病。
words.en: To confirm something means to establish its truth or validity by providing evidence or proof.

words.ex: The instructions are unambiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很清楚。
words.en: If you describe something as unambiguous, you mean that it is clear and cannot be misunderstood.

words.ex: Can you pronounce this word correctly?
words.ex_cn: 你能正确发音这个词吗？
words.en: To pronounce means to make the sound of a word or letter with your voice. It can also mean to declare or announce something officially or formally.

words.ex: The pope is considered infallible in matters of faith by some Catholics.
words.ex_cn: 一些天主教徒认为教皇在信仰问题上是一贯正确的。
words.en: If a person or thing is infallible, they are never wrong or never fail.

words.ex: He is undoubtedly the best student in class.
words.ex_cn: 他无疑是班上最好的学生。
words.en: Without doubt; certainly.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 物理状态

words.tr: adj. 活跃的；积极的；主动的；
words.ex: He is an active student in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上是一个活跃的学生。
words.en: Someone who is active moves around a lot or does a lot of things.

words.ex: She picked up the coil of rope from the ground.
words.ex_cn: 她从地上捡起了那卷绳子。
words.en: A coil is a length of something wound in a joined sequence of loops, or the act of winding something into loops.

words.ex: The spoon has a concave surface.
words.ex_cn: 勺子有一个凹的表面。
words.en: A concave surface is curved inward, like the inside of a bowl.

words.ex: The ball has a convex surface.
words.ex_cn: 这个球有一个凸出的表面。
words.en: A convex surface curves outward in the middle.

words.ex: The keys dangle from his belt.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙挂在他的腰带上。
words.en: If something dangles from somewhere or if you dangle it somewhere, it hangs or swings loosely.

words.ex: The book encompasses all basic math skills.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包含了所有基础数学技能。
words.en: If something encompasses particular things, it includes them.

words.tr:
n. （驼）峰；驼背；小土丘
v. 背负（重物）；弓起
words.ex: The camel has a big hump on its back.
words.ex_cn: 骆驼的背上有一个大驼峰。
words.en: A hump is a rounded protuberance or bulge, especially on the back of a camel or other animal, or on a person's back. As a verb, it means to form into a hump or to carry something with difficulty.

words.tr:
n. 音高；球场；程度（最高点）；宣传论点；
v. 扎营；
words.ex: The singer changed the pitch of her voice.
words.ex_cn: 歌手改变了她声音的音高。
words.en: Pitch can refer to the highness or lowness of a sound, the act of throwing something, or a thick, black, sticky substance used for paving roads or waterproofing.

words.tr:
n. 计划；方案；项目；课题；
v. 投射；预计；
words.ex: He presented his school project to the class.
words.ex_cn: 他向全班展示了他的学校计划。
words.en: A project is a piece of work that is planned or intended, or a large piece of work that is done by a group of people.

words.ex: The nail protrudes from the wood.
words.ex_cn: 钉子从木头里凸出来。
words.en: If something protrudes from somewhere, it sticks out.

words.tr: adv. 定期地；经常地；有规律地；
words.ex: He visits his grandparents regularly.
words.ex_cn: 他定期去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: At consistent intervals or in a consistent manner.

words.tr:
v. 滚动；
n. 滚动；卷形物；
words.ex: The ball roll down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 球从山上滚下来。
words.en: To move somewhere by turning over and over, or to make something move in this way.

words.ex: The wheel rotates slowly.
words.ex_cn: 轮子缓慢地转动。
words.en: To rotate means to turn or cause to turn around an axis or center.

words.ex: The roof has a sharp slant.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶有一个陡峭的倾斜。
words.en: If something slants or if you slant it, it is at an angle rather than being straight up and down or straight from side to side.

words.ex: The children played on the slope behind the house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房子后面的斜坡上玩耍。
words.en: A slope is a surface that is at an angle, so that one end is higher than the other.

words.tr:
n. 旋转；
v. 旋转；
words.ex: The spin of the top made it stay upright.
words.ex_cn: 陀螺的旋转让它保持直立。
words.en: If something spins or if you spin it, it turns quickly around a central point.

words.ex: The room was stuffy and hard to breathe in.
words.ex_cn: 房间闷热得让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a place as stuffy, you mean that it is unpleasantly warm and has no fresh air.

words.tr: adj. 倾斜的；v. 使倾斜（tilt 的过去分词）；
words.ex: The picture on the wall was tilted.
words.ex_cn: 墙上的画是倾斜的。
words.en: If something tilts or if you tilt it, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.

words.tr:
n. 塔；塔楼；
v. 高耸；
words.ex: The tower stands tall in the center of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这座塔矗立在城市中心。
words.en: A tower is a tall, narrow building, either part of a larger building such as a church or castle, or standing alone.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 状态变化

words.ex: The wind began to abate after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风开始减弱。
words.en: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: The amplifier gives amplification to the sound.
words.ex_cn: 放大器对声音进行放大。
words.en: The process of increasing the volume, extent, or significance of something.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.ex: The ascent of the mountain took all day.
words.ex_cn: 登这座山花了一整天。
words.en: An ascent is an act of climbing or moving upwards, or a path or slope that leads upwards.

words.ex: The heat made the metal deform.
words.ex_cn: 热量使金属变形。
words.en: To deform something means to change its shape, usually in a way that makes it less attractive or useful.

words.ex: The plane began its descent at 10,000 feet.
words.ex_cn: 飞机在一万英尺高度开始下降。
words.en: The act of moving or falling downward.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: Exercise can enhance your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提高你的健康。
words.en: To enhance something means to improve its value, quality, or attractiveness.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.tr: n. 扩展；延长期；延伸；电话分机；
words.ex: The company added an extension to its office building.
words.ex_cn: 公司为办公楼加了一个扩建部分。
words.en: An extension is a part that is added to something to make it longer or larger, or the act of adding this part.

words.tr:
n. 远足；
v. 远足；
words.ex: We went on a long hike in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 我们去山里进行了一次长途远足。
words.en: A hike is a long walk in the country, especially one that you go on for pleasure. It can also refer to an increase in the cost or amount of something.

words.ex: The workers used a hoist to lift the heavy beams.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用吊升机械吊起沉重的梁。
words.en: To hoist something means to lift or pull it up to a higher position, usually using some kind of equipment such as a crane or pulley.

words.ex: Practice can sharpen your skills.
words.ex_cn: 练习可以提高你的技能。
words.en: To make or become sharp or sharper.

words.tr:
v. 伸展；延伸；持续；
n. 一段；伸展；
words.ex: He stretches his arms every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上伸展手臂。
words.en: To stretch is to extend your body or a part of your body to its full length, or to extend something else to its full length or beyond its normal limits.

words.ex: The new teacher transformed the class into a lively group.
words.ex_cn: 这位新老师把班级变成了一个充满活力的团体。
words.en: To transform something or someone means to change them completely and usually improve their appearance, form, or structure.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 状态稳定

words.tr:
n. 平衡；姿态；镇静
v. 使平衡；保持（某种姿势）
words.ex: The dancer maintained her poise on one foot.
words.ex_cn: 舞者单脚保持平衡。
words.en: If someone has poise, they are calm, dignified, and self-controlled.

words.ex: The bridge is stable and safe to cross.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥很稳固，可以安全通过。
words.en: If something is stable, it is not likely to change or come to an end suddenly.

words.ex: The temperature rose steadily throughout the day.
words.ex_cn: 白天温度稳定地上升。
words.en: If something happens or changes steadily, it happens or changes in a regular way without interruption.

words.tr:
adj. 稳定的；
v. 使稳住；
words.ex: The boat moved in a steady way on the calm sea.
words.ex_cn: 船在平静的海面上平稳地移动。
words.en: If something is steady, it is firm and does not shake or move about. If you steady something, you stop it from shaking or moving about.

words.ex: The stability of the table prevents it from wobbling.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的固定防止它摇晃。
words.en: The state of being stable; the quality of being unchanging.

words.ex: The doctor tried to tranquilize the anxious patient.
words.ex_cn: 医生试图让焦虑的病人平静下来。
words.en: To tranquilize someone or an animal means to make them calm or unconscious, especially by giving them a drug.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 缩减

words.ex: The snake constricts its prey.
words.ex_cn: 蛇缠住它的猎物。
words.en: If something constricts you, it limits your actions so that you cannot do what you want to do.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.ex: The school will curtail recess time during exams.
words.ex_cn: 学校在考试期间将缩短课间休息时间。
words.en: If you curtail something, you reduce or limit it.

words.ex: His rude words detract from the beauty of the speech.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话贬损了演讲的优美。
words.en: If one thing detracts from another, it makes it seem less good or impressive.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.ex: The water in the pond dwindles in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天时，池塘里的水逐渐减少。
words.en: If something dwindles, it becomes smaller, weaker, or less in number.

words.tr:
v. 缩进排版；使呈锯齿状
n. 订货单
words.ex: Please indent the first line of each paragraph.
words.ex_cn: 请将每段的第一行缩进。
words.en: To start a line of text further from the margin than the main part of the text.

words.ex: We need to reduce waste in our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要减少日常生活中的浪费。
words.en: If you reduce something, you make it smaller in size or amount, or less in degree.

words.ex: The subtraction of 5 from 10 gives 5.
words.ex_cn: 10减去5等于5。
words.en: Subtraction is the process of taking one number or amount away from another.

words.tr:
adj. 狭窄的；窄小的；
v. 使窄小；
words.ex: The road is narrow and hard to drive on.
words.ex_cn: 这条路很窄，开车很难。
words.en: If something narrows, or if you narrow it, it becomes less wide.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after drinking.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制酒后驾驶。
words.en: to limit the movements or actions of someone, or to limit something and reduce its size or prevent it from increasing

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.tr:
n. 减少；
v. 减少；降低；
words.ex: There was a decrease in rainfall last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月降雨量减少了。
words.en: If something decreases or you decrease it, it becomes less in quantity, size, or intensity.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.ex: He deducts tax from his salary every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每月从工资中扣除税款。
words.en: If you deduct an amount from a total, you subtract it from the total.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 偶然

words.ex: He had an accidental fall while walking.
words.ex_cn: 他在走路时不小心摔了一跤。
words.en: An accidental event happens by chance, without being planned.

words.tr: adj. 随意的；非正式的；偶然的；
words.ex: He wore casual clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了随意的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behavior as casual, you mean they are not very concerned about what they are doing or what is happening around them, or they are not taking it seriously.

words.ex: The trip is contingent on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行取决于天气情况。
words.en: A contingent event or situation depends on something else in order to happen or exist.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.ex: It was fortuitous that he found his keys just before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他在出发前刚好找到钥匙，真是幸运。
words.en: If you describe something as fortuitous, you mean that it happens by chance rather than by anyone's planning or intention.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.ex: He bought a lottery ticket last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周买了一张彩票。
words.en: A lottery is a type of gambling game in which people buy numbered tickets. Several numbers are then chosen, and the people who have those numbers on their tickets win a prize.

words.ex: He makes occasional visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他偶尔去看望祖父母。
words.en: Occasional means happening or done sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.ex: He picked a random number to win the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他随意选了一个数字来赢得奖品。
words.en: If you describe something as random, you mean that it happens or is chosen without any definite plan, pattern, or purpose.

words.ex: I bought some milk, and incidentally, I saw your friend.
words.ex_cn: 我买了一些牛奶，顺便见到了你的朋友。
words.en: used to add something to what was said before, often something that you have just thought of

words.ex: The cost of lunch was incidental to the main expense.
words.ex_cn: 午餐的费用是主要开销的附带部分。
words.en: If one thing is incidental to another, it is less important than the other thing or is not a major part of it.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 衰弱

words.ex: The city showed signs of decadence after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这座城市显示出衰败的迹象。
words.en: Decadence is a situation in which a society or institution is becoming less moral and less satisfactory.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr:
adj. 退步的；堕落的；腐化的
v. 退化；堕落
n. 堕落的人
words.ex: The old machine became degenerate and stopped working.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器退步了，停止工作了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something degenerates, you mean that they become worse in some way, for example, poorer, weaker, or less respectable.

words.ex: The soil degrades over time without proper care.
words.ex_cn: 如果没有适当照料，土壤会逐渐退化。
words.en: If something degrades or is degraded, it becomes worse in quality, or weaker in power or status.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.tr:
n. 退潮；衰退；减少
v. 退潮；衰退；减少
words.ex: The ebb of the tide left fish on the sand.
words.ex_cn: 退潮把鱼留在了沙滩上。
words.en: The movement of the tide out to sea.

words.ex: The hot weather enervates him.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让他感到乏力。
words.en: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.ex: His debility was due to a long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱是由于长期患病。
words.en: Debility is a state of physical weakness, especially as a result of illness.

words.tr: adj. 虚弱的；衰弱的；无力的；
words.ex: The old man gave a feeble smile.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人露出虚弱的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as feeble, you mean that they are weak.

words.tr:
n. 腐烂；衰落；
v. 腐烂；
words.ex: The fruit began to show signs of decay.
words.ex_cn: 这水果开始出现腐烂的迹象。
words.en: To decay means to be slowly destroyed by a natural process or to become gradually worse in quality, condition, or strength.

words.ex: The flowers wither in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 花朵在烈日下枯萎。
words.en: If a plant withers, it dries up and dies. If something withers, it becomes weaker or less important until it disappears completely.

words.ex: The economy is in a recessionary phase.
words.ex_cn: 经济正处于衰退阶段。
words.en: Relating to or denoting a period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity are reduced, generally identified by a fall in GDP in two successive quarters.

words.tr:
v. 衰落；减弱；缺；亏
n. 衰退；减弱；缺；亏
words.ex: The moon begins to wane after the full moon.
words.ex_cn: 满月之后，月亮开始变暗。
words.en: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 缺乏

words.ex: The room was devoid of any furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间里全无家具。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is devoid of a quality or thing, you are emphasizing that they have none of it.

words.tr:
n. 没收物；罚金
v. 丧失；被没收
words.ex: He had to pay a forfeit for breaking the rule.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规定不得不支付没收物。
words.en: If you forfeit something, you lose it or are forced to give it up because you have broken a rule or done something wrong.

words.ex: The water supply is insufficient for the whole village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对整个村庄来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is insufficient, it is not enough for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He had a meager meal after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后吃了一顿很少的饭。
words.en: If you describe an amount or quantity of something as meager, you are critical of it because it is very small or not enough.

words.ex: The needy family received food from the charity.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫穷的家庭从慈善机构收到了食物。
words.en: Needy people do not have enough food, medicine, or clothing, or adequate houses.

words.tr: adj. 欠缺的；过小的；少量的
words.ex: He had scanty food for the whole day.
words.ex_cn: 他一整天的食物很少。
words.en: If something is scanty, there is not enough of it or it is too small in amount.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏的；不足的；稀有的；
words.ex: Water is scarce in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很缺乏。
words.en: If something is scarce, there is not enough of it.

words.ex: He is stingy with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很吝啬。
words.en: If you describe someone as stingy, you are criticizing them for being unwilling to spend money or to give or use a lot of something.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.tr: v. 缺乏；“lack”的现在分词； adj. 缺乏的；
words.ex: He is lacking confidence in speaking English.
words.ex_cn: 他在说英语时缺乏信心。
words.en: If something is lacking, there is not enough of it or it does not exist at all.

words.ex: The war impoverished many families.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使许多家庭变得贫困。
words.en: To make someone poor or to reduce the quality, strength, or richness of something.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；缺乏的；有缺陷的
words.ex: The plant is deficient in sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物缺乏阳光。
words.en: If someone or something is deficient in a particular thing, they do not have the full amount of it that they need.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏足够教育的；贫穷的； v. 剥夺；使丧失；“deprive”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: Children from deprived areas often struggle to read and write.
words.ex_cn: 来自教育缺乏地区的儿童常常难以阅读和写作。
words.en: If you are deprived of something that you want or need, you do not have it.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 频率

words.tr: adj. 永不停止的；连续不断的
words.ex: The rain fell in ceaseless drops all night.
words.ex_cn: 雨整晚不停地落下。
words.en: If something is ceaseless, it continues without stopping or without a pause.

words.tr: adj. 恒定的；不变的；持续的；
words.ex: The temperature is constant in this room.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间的温度是恒定的。
words.en: Something that is constant happens all the time or is always there.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；一阵阵的
words.ex: He had fitful sleep last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚睡得断断续续。
words.en: Something that is fitful happens for irregular periods of time or occurs at irregular times, rather than being continuous.

words.ex: The frequency of the radio station is 101.5 MHz.
words.ex_cn: 这个电台的频率是101.5兆赫。
words.en: The rate at which something happens or is repeated over a particular period of time.

words.ex: The memory of the accident still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故的记忆仍然长期困扰着他。
words.en: If something unpleasant haunts you, you keep thinking or worrying about it over a long period of time. A place that is haunted is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.tr: adj. 不断的；不停的；连续的
words.ex: The baby cried with incessant noise.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿不停地哭闹。
words.en: If you say that something is incessant, you are emphasizing that it continues without stopping.

words.tr: adj. 快的；迅速的；敏捷的；
words.ex: He gave a speedy reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题做出了快速的答复。
words.en: Something that is speedy moves or happens quickly.

words.ex: He won three successive championships.
words.ex_cn: 他连续赢得了三届冠军。
words.en: Following one after the other without interruption.

words.tr:
adj. 迅速的；敏捷的；快的；
n. 雨燕；
words.ex: The swift runner won the race.
words.ex_cn: 这位迅速的跑步者赢得了比赛。
words.en: moving or capable of moving at great speed, or happening within a very short time; fast.

words.ex: The continual rain made the road very muddy.
words.ex_cn: 不停的雨让道路变得非常泥泞。
words.en: Something that is continual happens repeatedly over a period of time.

words.tr:
adj. 有规律的；经常的；常见的；
n. 常客；
words.ex: He goes for a run every morning, a regular habit.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跑步，这是一个有规律的习惯。
words.en: Something that is regular happens or is done at equal intervals or is consistent in pattern or occurrence.

words.ex: He made a persistent effort to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他持续努力学习英语。
words.en: Continuing firmly or obstinately in a course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 黏附

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.tr:
n. 拥护者；信徒
adj. 黏附…的
words.ex: He is an adherent of the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 他是这项新政策的拥护者。
words.en: An adherent is someone who supports a particular party, person, or set of ideas.

words.tr: n. 依恋；附件；附加装置；
words.ex: The child showed strong attachment to his teddy bear.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对他的泰迪熊产生了强烈的依恋。
words.en: An attachment is a file that is sent along with an email message.

words.ex: The child clings to his mother's leg.
words.ex_cn: 孩子紧贴着妈妈的腿。
words.en: If you cling to someone or something, you hold onto them tightly.

words.tr: v. 黏合；连结；附着；连贯；形成整体
words.ex: The pieces cohere to form a complete picture.
words.ex_cn: 这些碎片组合在一起形成一幅完整的图画。
words.en: If the different elements of a piece of writing, a theory, or a policy cohere, they fit together well so that they form a united whole.

words.ex: The honey is sticky.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是黏的。
words.en: Something that is sticky is covered with a substance that things stick to.

words.tr:
v. 粘附；（随意）放置；忍受；
n. 棍枝；条状物；球棍；
words.ex: The glue makes the paper stick to the table.
words.ex_cn: 胶水使纸粘在桌子上。
words.en: A stick is a thin branch which has fallen off a tree. If you stick something somewhere, you put it there in a rather casual way.

words.ex: The rocks had a slabby surface from erosion.
words.ex_cn: 这些岩石因侵蚀而呈现出板状表面。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a slab; consisting of or containing slabs.

words.tr: v. 粘合；使（创口）愈合; adj. 粘合的
words.ex: The glue will conglutinate the paper pieces.
words.ex_cn: 胶水会把纸片粘在一起。
words.en: To cause to adhere or stick together; to coalesce.

words.tr: v. 黏合，被黏合；凝集，（使）凝集；（语言）粘着; n. 胶结产物; adj. 粘结的
words.ex: The glue will agglutinate the paper pieces together.
words.ex_cn: 胶水会把纸片粘在一起。
words.en: To cause to adhere, as with glue; to unite or cause to coalesce.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 扩大

words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.ex: Reading books can broaden your mind.
words.ex_cn: 读书可以扩大你的视野。
words.en: If something broadens or if you broaden it, it increases in size or range.

words.ex: The doctor used drops to dilate her pupils.
words.ex_cn: 医生用了滴眼液来扩大她的瞳孔。
words.en: If you dilate something such as a part of your body, or if it dilates, it becomes larger or wider.

words.tr: v. 扩大；膨胀；更充分地阐述；
words.ex: The company plans to expand its business to other countries.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划将其业务扩大到其他国家。
words.en: To increase in size, number, or importance, or to make something increase in this way.

words.ex: The city's sprawl has covered many farmlands.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市的杂乱无序的拓展覆盖了许多农田。
words.en: If you sprawl somewhere, you sit or lie with your legs and arms spread out in a careless way.

words.ex: The wound began to swell after the insect bite.
words.ex_cn: 被昆虫叮咬后，伤口开始肿胀。
words.en: To increase in size or volume as a result of internal pressure; to expand.

words.ex: The company plans to enlarge its office space.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划扩大其办公空间。
words.en: To make something bigger or more extensive.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: He outstretched his arms to hug her.
words.ex_cn: 他伸开双臂去拥抱她。
words.en: To outstretch means to extend or stretch out something, especially an arm or a hand, to reach or grab something.

words.tr:
v. 促进；使增长；
n. 提高；增强；
words.ex: Exercise can boost your energy.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进你的精力。
words.en: If one thing boosts another, it causes it to increase, improve, or be more successful.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 聚集

words.ex: He will assemble the toy for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他将为儿子组装玩具。
words.en: If people assemble or if someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

words.ex: The assembly of the car took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的装配花了三天时间。
words.en: An assembly is a group of people gathered together for a particular purpose, such as a meeting or a legislative session. It can also refer to the process of fitting together the component parts of a machine or other object.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: People gather in the square for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 人们在广场上聚集庆祝节日。
words.en: If people gather somewhere, or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: He amass wealth by working hard.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力工作积累财富。
words.en: If you amass something such as money or information, you gradually collect a large amount of it.

words.tr:
n. （鸟或羊）群；（人）群；
v. 聚集；群集；
words.ex: A flock of birds flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 一群鸟飞过田野。
words.en: A flock is a group of birds, sheep, or goats, or a large group of people. It can also refer to a soft material for stuffing cushions, quilts, etc., made from wool or cotton. As a verb, it means to gather or move in a flock.

words.ex: The music accompanies the dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐伴随舞蹈。
words.en: To go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort; to play a musical accompaniment for.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 混乱

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使混乱；使烂醉
words.ex: The complicated instructions befuddle him.
words.ex_cn: 这些复杂的说明让他困惑。
words.en: If something befuddles you, it confuses your mind or thoughts.

words.tr:
adj. 复杂的；
n. 综合楼（群）；
words.ex: The instructions are too complex for children.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明对孩子来说太复杂了。
words.en: Something that is complex has many different parts, and is therefore often difficult to understand.

words.ex: Too many rules can complicate the game.
words.ex_cn: 太多的规则会使游戏变得复杂。
words.en: To make something more difficult to understand or deal with by adding more parts or details.

words.ex: The instructions confuse me.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明让我感到困惑。
words.en: If you confuse two things, you mix them up in your mind so that you think one is the other.

words.tr:
v. 弄乱；使混乱
n. 无秩序；混乱；衣冠不整
words.ex: The storm disarrayed the books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把书架上的书弄乱了。
words.en: a state of disorganization or untidiness

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使糊涂；胡乱应付
n. 混乱；糊涂
words.ex: He muddled the instructions and got confused.
words.ex_cn: 他把说明搞混了，感到困惑。
words.en: If you muddle things or people, you get them mixed up, so that you do not know which is which.

words.tr:
v. 拖曳；搅乱；洗牌；移来移去
n. 拖着脚走；洗牌；混在一起
words.ex: He shuffle his feet across the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他拖着脚在地板上走。
words.en: To shuffle is to walk by dragging one's feet along or without lifting them fully from the ground. It also means to mix up the order of things, especially cards in a deck.

words.ex: The room was in chaos after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对之后，房间一片混乱。
words.en: A state of complete disorder and confusion.

words.tr: n. 混乱；难懂的话；嘈杂声
words.ex: His speech was pure babelism, no one understood him.
words.ex_cn: 他的讲话完全是胡言乱语，没人听得懂。
words.en: A state of confusion or disorder, especially in speech or sound, reminiscent of the Tower of Babel.

words.ex: The room was in complete disorder.
words.ex_cn: 房间一片混乱。
words.en: A disorder is a state of confusion or untidiness, or a medical problem that affects the mind or body.

words.tr: n. 混乱；动荡；骚乱；恐慌
words.ex: The storm caused turmoil in the town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty.

words.tr:
n. 杂乱；混乱
v. 弄乱
words.ex: The table is full of clutter.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上堆满了杂物。
words.en: If things or people clutter a place, they fill it in an untidy way.

words.tr:
v. （使）纠缠；使陷入；使混乱
n. 纠缠；混乱；纠纷
words.ex: The cat got into a tangle with the yarn.
words.ex_cn: 猫和毛线缠在一起了。
words.en: If something is tangled or tangles, it becomes twisted together in an untidy way.

words.tr: n. 混乱；骚乱情景；疯人院
words.ex: The classroom was a bedlam during the fire drill.
words.ex_cn: 火灾演习时，教室里一片混乱。
words.en: A scene of uproar and confusion.

words.tr: n. 喧嚣；大混乱；大吵大闹
words.ex: The crowd created pandemonium when the winner was announced.
words.ex_cn: 当获胜者被宣布时，人群陷入了混乱。
words.en: Pandemonium is a situation in which there is a lot of noise and confusion because people are excited, angry, or frightened.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 恢复

words.tr: v. 赋予能量；使精力充沛；激励
words.ex: Coffee helps me energize in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 咖啡帮助我在早上恢复活力。
words.en: To energize someone means to give them the enthusiasm, determination, and energy to do something.

words.tr:
v. 集合起来；振作；复苏
n. 集会
words.ex: The crowd rallied to support their team.
words.ex_cn: 人群聚集起来支持他们的球队。
words.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party or a sports team. It can also mean to come together again in order to continue fighting or arguing after a defeat or a period of confusion.

words.tr: v. 恢复；重新获得；复原；
words.ex: He will recover from the illness soon.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就会从疾病中恢复。
words.en: If you recover from an illness or an injury, you become well again. If you recover something that has been lost or stolen, you find it or get it back.

words.tr: v. 使恢复精力；使复原；使变新
words.ex: A short nap can refresh you.
words.ex_cn: 小睡一会儿能让你恢复精力。
words.en: To refresh someone means to make them feel less tired or less hot.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.ex: He will restore the old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他将修复这辆旧自行车。
words.en: To restore something means to bring it back to its original condition or to a state of health, efficiency, or good management.

words.ex: He went back to retrieve his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他回去取回他的钥匙。
words.en: To retrieve something means to get it back from somewhere, especially after it has been lost or taken away.

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.ex: The teacher will revoke his privilege to use the computer.
words.ex_cn: 老师将撤销他使用电脑的权限。
words.en: If someone in authority revokes something such as a law, license, or agreement, they cancel it.

words.ex: After a short break, he resumed his work.
words.ex_cn: 短暂休息后，他继续工作。
words.en: If you resume an activity or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after an interruption.

words.ex: He needs time to recuperate after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他需要时间在手术后恢复。
words.en: To recuperate means to recover from illness or exertion, or to regain or make up for something lost or damaged.

words.tr: v. 使年轻； 使恢复精神； 使复原
words.ex: The new sleep routine helps rejuvenate her energy.
words.ex_cn: 新的睡眠习惯帮助她恢复精力。
words.en: To rejuvenate someone or something means to make them look or feel young, fresh, or lively again.

words.tr: v. 逐步康复；渐愈；复原
words.ex: He is convalescing at home after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后在家休养。
words.en: To convalesce means to recover health and strength gradually after sickness or weakness.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 缓和

words.ex: She drank water to assuage her thirst.
words.ex_cn: 她喝水来缓解口渴。
words.en: If you assuage an unpleasant feeling that someone has, you make them feel it less strongly. To assuage a problem or situation means to make it less intense or severe.

words.tr:
v. 安慰；慰问
n. 控制台；操纵台
words.ex: She whispered kind words to console her crying friend.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声说些安慰的话来安抚哭泣的朋友。
words.en: If you console someone who is unhappy about something, you try to make them feel more cheerful.

words.ex: She put a cushion on the chair to make it comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她在椅子上放了一个靠垫，让它更舒服。
words.en: A cushion is a soft bag of some ornamental material, stuffed with wool, hair, feathers, polyester staple fiber, non-woven material, or even paper torn into fragments. It may be used for sitting or kneeling upon, or to soften the hardness or angularity of a chair or couch.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.ex: He tried to mollify his angry friend with an apology.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用道歉来安抚他生气的朋友。
words.en: To mollify someone means to make them feel calmer and less angry, upset, or worried.

words.ex: He tried to pacify the crying baby with a toy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个玩具让哭闹的婴儿安静下来。
words.en: If you pacify someone who is angry, upset, or not pleased, you make them calm or content.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.ex: He listens to music to relax.
words.ex_cn: 他听音乐来放松。
words.en: If you relax or if something relaxes you, you feel more calm and less worried or tense.

words.ex: The wind began to slacken after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风速开始减缓。
words.en: If something slackens or if you slacken it, it becomes slower, less active, or less intense.

words.tr: v. 使安静；安慰；使缓和
words.ex: She sang a song to soothe the baby.
words.ex_cn: 她唱了一首歌来安抚婴儿。
words.en: To soothe someone means to make them feel calmer and less anxious, upset, or angry.

words.ex: The wind began to abate after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴过后，风开始减弱。
words.en: If something bad or undesirable abates, it becomes much less strong or severe.

words.tr: adj. 缓和（炎症）的，镇痛的; n. （治疗炎症的）缓和剂，镇痛剂
words.ex: Honey is a demulcent for a sore throat.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜对喉咙痛有舒缓作用。
words.en: A demulcent is a substance that relieves irritation of the mucous membranes in the mouth by forming a protective film.

words.tr: n. 缓和剂；润泽药; adj. 缓和的；减轻痛苦的
words.ex: The lenitive medicine eased her pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种舒缓的药物减轻了她的疼痛。
words.en: A lenitive is something that has the effect of easing pain or discomfort.

words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.ex: Drugs can relieve pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To relieve someone or something means to make a problem, pain, or unpleasant feeling less severe or to take it away completely.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 分离

words.ex: He tried to detach himself from the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图脱离这个群体。
words.en: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.

words.tr: adj. 分离的； v. 脱离；拆卸；分离；“detach”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house is detached from the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子与邻居的房子是分开的。
words.en: If someone is detached, they do not have any emotional interest in a situation and therefore can make fair decisions.

words.tr: v. 使分离；使分裂；使不和
words.ex: The conflict disunited the once harmonious community.
words.ex_cn: 冲突使得曾经和谐的社区变得不和。
words.en: To cause to be no longer united or in agreement; to divide.

words.tr: v. 撕碎；劈开；揪扯；割裂
words.ex: The storm rends the tree from its roots.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨将树从根部撕裂。
words.en: To tear or split something apart with great force.

words.ex: The wind scatter the leaves everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得四处分散。
words.en: To scatter means to throw or drop things over a wide area in an irregular way, or to cause a group of people or animals to move apart in different directions.

words.ex: The school used to segregate students by race.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去按种族隔离学生。
words.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people, animals, or things from another, especially because they are of different types or belong to different categories.

words.tr: v. 切断；脱离；切成两段
words.ex: He severed the rope with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀把绳子割断了。
words.en: To sever something means to cut through it or to break it off completely.

words.ex: He enjoys solitude in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在森林中独处。
words.en: The state or situation of being alone.

words.ex: The two houses are apart by fifty meters.
words.ex_cn: 这两所房子相隔五十米。
words.en: If people or things are apart, they are separated by a distance.

words.tr: v. 解开；分离；使解脱；脱离战斗
words.ex: He tried to disengage from the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从争论中抽身。
words.en: To disengage means to separate or detach oneself from something or someone, or to release from a connection or obligation.

words.ex: Sugar dissolves in water.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中溶解。
words.en: If a substance dissolves in liquid or if you dissolve a substance, it becomes mixed with the liquid and disappears.

words.tr:
adj. 分开的；分离的；单独的；
v. 分离；隔离；
words.ex: They live in separate houses.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在分开的房子里。
words.en: To cause to move or be apart; to divide or keep apart.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 发展

words.tr: adj. 技艺高超的；完成的；熟练的； v. 完成；实现；“accomplish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is an accomplished pianist.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位技艺高超的钢琴家。
words.en: If someone is accomplished at something, they are very skilled at it.

words.tr: v. 完成；实现；达到；获得；
words.ex: He worked hard to achieve his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以完成他的目标。
words.en: To achieve something means to reach a particular goal or result through effort, skill, or courage.

words.tr:
n. 发展；进步；提前；
adj. 预先的；在前的；
v. 前进；发展；提前；
words.ex: The advance of technology has changed our lives.
words.ex_cn: 科技的发展改变了我们的生活。
words.en: If you advance a cause, interest, or claim, you support it and help it to succeed.

words.ex: His pride begets conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他的骄傲招致了冲突。
words.en: To beget means to cause something to happen or exist.

words.ex: The climax of the movie was a big chase scene.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的高潮是一场大追捕场景。
words.en: The climax is the most exciting or important part of a play, film, or piece of music, which usually happens near the end.

words.ex: The class will commence at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程将在上午9点开始。
words.en: To begin something; to start.

words.ex: He concluded that the experiment failed.
words.ex_cn: 他得出结论说实验失败了。
words.en: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

words.tr: adj. 无可置疑的；决定性的；
words.ex: The evidence was conclusive.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可置疑的。
words.en: If something is conclusive, it means that it proves something in a way that is certain and leaves no doubt.

words.ex: His condition improved after the treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他的状况在接受治疗后好转了。
words.en: A condition is a state of affairs that must exist or be brought about before something else can happen or be done.

words.ex: The concert was the culmination of his music career.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会是他音乐生涯的顶点。
words.en: The culmination of something is the highest or final point of it, often after a long period of development.

words.ex: The country is developing its economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在发展它的经济。
words.en: To develop means to grow or cause to grow and become more mature, advanced, or elaborate.

words.ex: A bird emerged from the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一只鸟从树中浮现出来。
words.en: If something or someone emerges, they come out of or move out of something and become visible.

words.ex: Poverty can engender crime.
words.ex_cn: 贫困会引起犯罪。
words.en: To cause a feeling, situation, or condition to exist.

words.ex: The eventual winner was a young student.
words.ex_cn: 最后的赢家是一位年轻学生。
words.en: An eventual event or situation happens at the end of a process or period of time.

words.ex: The exit is near the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 出口在楼梯附近。
words.en: To exit means to go out of or leave a place.

words.tr:
adj. 最终的；最后的；
n. 决赛；
words.ex: This is the final answer.
words.ex_cn: 这是最终的答案。
words.en: Last in a series or coming at the end of a process.

words.tr:
adj. 最重要的；
adv. 首要地；
words.ex: He is the foremost expert in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的专家。
words.en: Most important or prominent; leading.

words.ex: The wind generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 风产生电力。
words.en: To generate something means to cause it to begin and develop.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.tr: n. 前进；进展；间隔时间
words.ex: He made headway in solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决这道数学题上取得了进展。
words.en: If you make headway, you progress towards achieving something.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.tr:
adj. 最初的；开始的；
n. 首字母；
words.ex: This is the initial plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个项目的最初计划。
words.en: The first letter of a name or word, used to represent the whole name or word.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.ex: The onset of winter brought heavy snow.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的开始带来了大雪。
words.en: The onset of something is the beginning of it, especially something unpleasant.

words.tr:
adj. 原来的；有创造性的；原版的；新颖的；
n. 原件；原稿；
words.ex: This is the original book I bought last year.
words.ex_cn: 这是我去年买的那本原版书。
words.en: An original piece of writing or music was written recently and has not been published or performed before.

words.ex: Originally, he wanted to be a teacher.
words.ex_cn: 起初，他想当一名老师。
words.en: Initially; in the first place; in a novel or inventive manner.

words.tr:
n. 高峰；顶峰；
v. 达到高峰；达到最高值；
words.ex: The mountain peak is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 这座山的高峰被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or level of something; the pointed top of a mountain.

words.tr:
n. 阶段；时期；
v. 分阶段进行；
words.ex: The project is in its final phase.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正处于最后阶段。
words.en: A phase is a particular stage in a process or in the gradual development of something.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；小学的；初等的；原来的；最初的；
words.ex: Primary goal is to stay safe.
words.ex_cn: 首要目标是保持安全。
words.en: Something that is primary is more important than anything else.

words.ex: After the break, we will proceed with the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 休息后，我们将继续开会。
words.en: If you proceed to do something, you continue to do it or start to do it after doing something else first.

words.tr:
n. 工序；过程；
v. 处理；加工；
words.ex: The factory improved the production process.
words.ex_cn: 工厂改进了生产工序。
words.en: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

words.tr: n. 进展；进步；缓慢前进；稳步前进；
words.ex: The project shows slow progress.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目进展缓慢。
words.en: Progress is the process of gradually improving or getting nearer to achieving or completing something.

words.tr:
n. 结果；
v. 导致；
words.ex: The result of the test was good.
words.ex_cn: 这次测试的结果很好。
words.en: A consequence, outcome, or effect of an action or situation.

words.ex: After a short break, he resumed his work.
words.ex_cn: 短暂休息后，他继续工作。
words.en: If you resume an activity or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after an interruption.

words.ex: His status in the company is very high.
words.ex_cn: 他在公司里的地位很高。
words.en: The status of someone or something is their position or situation according to the law or according to other people's opinions.

words.ex: He is a successful businessman.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成功的商人。
words.en: Achieving the results wanted or hoped for.

words.ex: The teacher will terminate the class at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下午5点结束课程。
words.en: To terminate something means to bring it to an end or to stop it from continuing.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

words.tr: v. 销声匿迹；突然消失；
words.ex: The magic trick made the coin vanish.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让硬币销声匿迹了。
words.en: If someone or something vanishes, they disappear suddenly or in a way that cannot be explained.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 穿透

words.ex: The knight was impaled on the spear.
words.ex_cn: 骑士被长矛刺穿了。
words.en: To impale someone or something means to pierce them with a sharp object such as a spear or spike.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.tr: v. （将刀剑）入鞘；放进套里；包；覆盖
words.ex: He sheathes his knife after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后把刀收进刀鞘。
words.en: To put something, especially a weapon, into a sheath; to cover or protect something with a sheath.

words.tr:
n. 刺；戳
v. 刺；戳
words.ex: He felt a sharp stab in his side.
words.ex_cn: 他感到侧腹一阵刺痛。
words.en: If someone stabs you, they push a knife or sharp object into your body.

words.tr: v. 刺穿；戳穿；使吓呆；使发愣
words.ex: The spike transfixes the wooden board.
words.ex_cn: 钉子刺穿了木板。
words.en: If you are transfixed by something, it holds your attention completely and you cannot think of anything else.

words.tr:
n. 刺刀；卡销
v. 用刺刀刺
words.ex: The soldier fixed a bayonet to his rifle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵把刺刀装到了步枪上。
words.en: A bayonet is a long, sharp blade that can be attached to the end of a rifle and used as a weapon in close combat.

words.ex: The spy tried to infiltrate the enemy base.
words.ex_cn: 间谍试图渗透敌方基地。
words.en: To enter or gain access to (an organization, place, etc.) surreptitiously and gradually, especially in order to acquire secret information.

words.tr:
n. 刺穿；刺孔
v. 刺穿；削弱
words.ex: The bike tire has a puncture.
words.ex_cn: 自行车轮胎有一个漏气孔。
words.en: A puncture is a small hole made by a sharp object, especially in a tire. To puncture something means to make a hole in it with a sharp object.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 冲突（竞争）

words.ex: The teacher admonished the student to finish his homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师劝告学生完成作业。
words.en: To admonish someone means to tell them in a serious way that they have done something wrong.

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

words.tr: v. 攻击；困扰；抨击；袭击
words.ex: The storm assailed the small village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴袭击了这个小村庄。
words.en: If someone assails you, they attack you violently, either physically or with words.

words.tr: v. （烤肉时）润以脂油；狠揍；殴打；大骂；公开责骂
words.ex: She baste the turkey with butter every 20 minutes.
words.ex_cn: 她每20分钟用黄油给火鸡刷一遍。
words.en: To baste means to sew with long, loose stitches in order to hold something in place temporarily, or to moisten meat or other food while cooking by spooning or brushing liquid over it.

words.tr:
adj. 交战的；寻衅的；好战的
n. 交战国；交战团体
words.ex: The two belligerent nations signed a peace treaty.
words.ex_cn: 这两个交战国家签署了和平条约。
words.en: A belligerent person or country is aggressive and eager to fight.

words.ex: Two companies compete for the same customers.
words.ex_cn: 两家公司为争夺相同的客户而竞争。
words.en: If you compete with someone for something, you try to get it for yourself and stop the other person getting it. You can also say that two people compete for something that they both want.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.ex: The two roads diverge after the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 两条路在桥后分岔。
words.en: If one thing diverges from another similar thing, the first thing becomes different from the second or develops differently from it. You can also say that two things diverge.

words.tr: adj. 分歧的；发散的；趋异的；
words.ex: The two friends had divergent opinions about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 这两个朋友对这部电影的看法不同。
words.en: If two things diverge, they are different from each other, or they become different from each other.

words.ex: He works hard to emulate his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他努力赶上他的哥哥。
words.en: To emulate someone or something means to try to be like them or to do something in the same way that they do it.

words.ex: The two families have a long feud.
words.ex_cn: 这两个家族有长期的世仇。
words.en: A feud is a prolonged and bitter quarrel or dispute, especially between two families or groups, often involving violence.

words.tr:
v. 皱眉；蹙额
n. 皱眉；蹙额
words.ex: He frowns when he hears bad news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到坏消息时会皱眉。
words.en: If you frown, you bring your eyebrows together so that there are lines on your face above your eyes, often because you are annoyed or worried.

words.tr: v. 大声呵斥；强烈谴责
words.ex: He fulminates against unfair laws.
words.ex_cn: 他强烈谴责不公正的法律。
words.en: To fulminate means to express vehement protest. It can also mean to explode or detonate.

words.ex: The hostile neighbor shouted at us every morning.
words.ex_cn: 那个敌意的邻居每天早上都对我们大喊大叫。
words.en: If you are hostile to another person or an idea, you disagree with them or disapprove of them, often showing this in your behavior.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.tr: adj. 冒犯的；令人不快的；进攻性的；
words.ex: His offensive words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他冒犯的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as offensive, you mean that it is rude or insulting.

words.tr:
adj. 平行的；
n. 类似的事物；
words.ex: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
words.ex_cn: 这两条线是平行的，永远不会相交。
words.en: Something that is parallel to something else is similar to it in many ways, or happens at the same time as it.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.ex: The smell repels insects.
words.ex_cn: 这种气味能击退昆虫。
words.en: If something repels you, it is so unpleasant or offensive that you want to avoid it or push it away.

words.tr:
v. 击退；回绝；憎恶
n. 拒斥；击退；严拒
words.ex: The soldiers repulse the enemy attack.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们击退了敌人的进攻。
words.en: If you repulse someone, you reject them or make them feel disgusted.

words.ex: The smell of the garbage is repulsive.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的气味令人厌恶。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as repulsive, you mean that they are horrible and disgusting and you want to avoid them.

words.tr:
n. 竞争者；敌手；
v. 竞争；相匹敌；
words.ex: He is my main rival in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他是我在比赛中主要的竞争者。
words.en: A rival is a person, group, or organization that you are competing with in the same activity or the same area.

words.ex: There is strife between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有争执。
words.en: Strife is angry or violent conflict between two people or groups.

words.tr:
n. 袭击；罢工；
v. 击打；侵袭；突然想到；
words.ex: The strike on the base happened at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 对基地的袭击发生在黎明时分。
words.en: To hit someone or something forcefully; to stop work as a form of protest.

words.tr:
v. 努力；斗争；挣扎；
n. 努力；斗争；难事；
words.ex: He struggles to finish his homework every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都努力完成作业。
words.en: If you struggle to do something, you try hard to do it, even though it is difficult or other people are making it difficult for you.

words.tr: v. （以可望而不可及之物）逗引；使干着急
words.ex: The smell of cookies tantalize him.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味让他垂涎欲滴。
words.en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have it.

words.tr:
v. 重击；捶击；发撞击声
n. 重击声；重打
words.ex: He thumped the table with his fist.
words.ex_cn: 他用拳头重击了桌子。
words.en: If you thump something, you hit it hard, usually with your fist.

chapters.name: Word List 35 状态 变化

words.ex: He converts old paper into new notebooks.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧纸张转换成新笔记本。
words.en: To change something into a different form or to change someone's beliefs, especially their religious beliefs.

words.ex: He wrote copious notes during the lecture.
words.ex_cn: 他在讲座期间写了大量的笔记。
words.en: Something that is copious exists in large amounts.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.ex: The company plans to diversify its products.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划使产品多样化。
words.en: To diversify means to make or become more varied or different. It often refers to the process of a company or individual expanding their range of products or activities to reduce risk or to explore new opportunities.

words.ex: The new job enriched his life.
words.ex_cn: 这份新工作使他的生活富裕起来。
words.en: To enrich something means to improve its quality, often by adding something to it.

words.tr: adj. 易变的；无常的；感情不专的
words.ex: He is fickle and changes his mind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他善变，每天都会改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as fickle, you disapprove of them because they keep changing their mind about what they like or want.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.ex: The garden has manifold flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有繁多的花朵。
words.en: If something is manifold, it has many different parts, features, or forms.

words.ex: The mutation caused the plant to grow differently.
words.ex_cn: 这种突变使植物的生长方式发生了变化。
words.en: A mutation is a change in the structure of the genes of an organism that results in a variant form which may be transmitted to subsequent generations, caused by the alteration of single base units in DNA, or the deletion, insertion, or rearrangement of larger sections of genes or chromosomes.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；不吝惜的；浪费的
words.ex: He was profuse in thanks after the rescue.
words.ex_cn: 获救后，他表达了深深的感谢。
words.en: If you describe something as profuse, you mean that it is very plentiful or abundant.

words.ex: The new teacher transformed the class into a lively group.
words.ex_cn: 这位新老师把班级变成了一个充满活力的团体。
words.en: To transform something or someone means to change them completely and usually improve their appearance, form, or structure.

words.ex: The transition from school to work was hard for him.
words.ex_cn: 从学校到工作的转变对他来说很难。
words.en: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.

words.ex: This apple is a variant of the red delicious.
words.ex_cn: 这种苹果是红富士的一个变体。
words.en: A variant is something that is slightly different from other similar things.

words.ex: The weather shows a lot of variation in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天天气变化很大。
words.en: A variation is a difference or change in the usual or expected amount, level, or form of something.

words.tr: adj. 各种各样的；不同的；各种的；
words.ex: He bought various fruits at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了各种各样的水果。
words.en: If you say that there are various things, you mean there are several different things of the type mentioned.

words.ex: The weather varies from day to day.
words.ex_cn: 天气每天都在变化。
words.en: If things vary, they are different from each other in size, amount, or degree.

chapters.name: Word List 36 语言 争辩

words.tr:
v. 斗嘴；闪烁
n. 口角
words.ex: They bicker over small things every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为小事争吵。
words.en: If people bicker, they argue or quarrel about unimportant things.

words.ex: The brawl started over a simple misunderstanding.
words.ex_cn: 这场争吵源于一个简单的误解。
words.en: A brawl is a rough or noisy fight or quarrel.

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.ex: His words were contradictory.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are contradictory, they state or imply that opposite things are true.

words.ex: He contravenes the school rules by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: To contravene a law or rule means to do something that is forbidden by it.

words.ex: The movie is controversial because it shows violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影因为展示暴力而有争议。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as controversial, you mean that they are the subject of intense public argument, disagreement, or disapproval.

words.ex: There was a controversy about the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 关于新校规，人们展开了争论。
words.en: A controversy is a disagreement or argument about something that involves many people and generates strong feelings.

words.ex: He controverts the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: To argue about (a subject) in a formal manner; to dispute or contradict.

words.ex: It is debatable whether he is the best player.
words.ex_cn: 他是不是最好的球员是有争议的。
words.en: If you say that something is debatable, you mean that it is not certain whether it is true or right.

words.tr:
v. 辩论；争论
n. 辩论；争论
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.

words.ex: He tried to disprove the theory with new data.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用新数据驳斥这个理论。
words.en: To disprove something means to show that it is not true or correct.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.ex: His eloquence moved everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的雄辩打动了房间里每一个人。
words.en: The ability to speak or write in a way that is fluent, persuasive, and expressive.

words.tr: adj. 雄辩的；有口才的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave an eloquent speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了富有感染力的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as eloquent, you mean that they are able to express their ideas and opinions well, so that other people understand them and are influenced by them.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr:
v. 争论；讲价
n. 讨价还价；争论
words.ex: They haggle over the price of the car.
words.ex_cn: 他们为汽车的价格争论。
words.en: If you haggle, you argue about something, especially about the price of something you want to buy.

words.ex: He refuted the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。
words.en: To prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false; to deny the truth or accuracy of something.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.tr:
n. 争吵
v. 争吵
words.ex: The two boys squabble over toys every day.
words.ex_cn: 这两个男孩每天为玩具争吵。
words.en: A squabble is a noisy disagreement about something unimportant.

words.tr:
v. 争论；争执；吵架
n. 争吵；口角
words.ex: They wrangle over the price every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为价格争执。
words.en: If you wrangle with someone, you argue with them in a noisy or angry way.

words.ex: He is a dissentious person who always argues with others.
words.ex_cn: 他是个好争论的人，总是和别人争吵。
words.en: Inclined to or causing dissent; contentious.

words.tr:
v. 争吵；吵架；
n. 争吵；口角；
words.ex: They quarrel over small things every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为小事争吵。
words.en: A quarrel is an angry argument or disagreement between people.

words.ex: He opposes the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这项新法律。
words.en: If you oppose someone or something, you disagree with them and try to prevent them from doing something, or you try to change what they are doing.

words.tr:
n. 挑战；
v. 提出挑战；
words.ex: Climbing that mountain is a big challenge.
words.ex_cn: 爬那座山是一个巨大的挑战。
words.en: A challenge is something new and difficult which requires great effort and determination.

words.tr: adj. 好争吵的；有争议的
words.ex: The plan is contentious because many people disagree.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划有争议，因为很多人不同意。
words.en: If you describe something as contentious, you mean that it is the subject of intense argument and disagreement.

words.ex: He rebut the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: If you rebut a charge or criticism that is made against you, you give reasons why it is untrue or unacceptable.

words.tr:
n. 柜台；
v. 抵消；反驳；
adv. 相反地；
words.ex: The customer paid at the counter.
words.ex_cn: 顾客在柜台付款。
words.en: A counter is a long flat surface in a shop or bank on which customers are served. It can also refer to a device that counts something, or an action taken to oppose something.

words.ex: He gave a quick rejoinder to her question.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的问题迅速做出了回应。
words.en: A rejoinder is a reply, especially a quick or witty one, to a question or remark.

words.ex: They had a tiff over the last piece of cake.
words.ex_cn: 他们为了最后一块蛋糕拌了几句嘴。
words.en: A tiff is a small unimportant quarrel, especially between two people who are usually friends or who are married to each other.

chapters.name: Word List 36 语言 协商

words.ex: He will consult a doctor for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他将咨询医生治疗他的头痛。
words.en: to seek information or advice from someone, especially someone who is an expert in a particular field

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.ex: The two countries made a pact to stop fighting.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家达成了一项停止战斗的协议。
words.en: A pact is a formal agreement between two or more people, organizations, or governments to do a particular thing or to help each other.

words.ex: He gave her flowers to placate her.
words.ex_cn: 他送她花来安抚她。
words.en: If you placate someone, you do or say something to make them stop feeling angry.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.ex: The two friends reached reconciliation after talking for hours.
words.ex_cn: 两个朋友经过几个小时的交谈后和好了。
words.en: Reconciliation is the process of making two opposite beliefs, ideas, or situations agree.

chapters.name: Word List 36 语言 谈话

words.tr: v. （贸然）上前搭讪；（唐突地）走近谈话
words.ex: He accosted a stranger on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他在街上拦住了一位陌生人。
words.en: If someone accosts another person, they go up to them and speak to them, especially in a way that seems rude or threatening.

words.tr: v. 哄；用好话劝诱；哄骗
words.ex: He tried to coax the cat out from under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄猫从床底下出来。
words.en: To coax someone means to persuade them to do something by gentle persuasion or flattery.

words.ex: He uses colloquial words when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时使用口语化的词语。
words.en: Colloquial language is informal language that is used in ordinary conversation rather than in writing or formal speech.

words.tr:
v. 称赞；恭维
n. 称赞；恭维
words.ex: He gave her a compliment on her dress.
words.ex_cn: 他夸了她的裙子。
words.en: A compliment is a polite expression of praise or admiration.

words.ex: She confides in her best friend.
words.ex_cn: 她向最好的朋友倾诉。
words.en: If you confide in someone, you tell them a secret.

words.tr: v. 慷慨陈词；高声朗诵
words.ex: He likes to declaim poetry in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在全班面前朗诵诗歌。
words.en: To declaim means to speak or recite something in a dramatic or impassioned way, often in public.

words.ex: The dialogue in the movie was very funny.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影中的对白非常幽默。
words.en: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people in a book, play, or film.

words.ex: He gave a dumb answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个愚笨的回答。
words.en: If someone is dumb, they are unable to speak. If you describe someone or something as dumb, you mean that they are stupid or silly.

words.ex: The hot lava effused from the volcano.
words.ex_cn: 熔岩从火山中流出。
words.en: To pour out or emit something, especially a liquid, light, or smell, in a steady flow.

words.tr: v. 含糊其辞；说模棱两可的话
words.ex: He equivocates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他含糊其辞。
words.en: If you equivocate, you use ambiguous language in order to deceive people or to avoid speaking directly about something.

words.ex: Please excuse me for being late.
words.ex_cn: 请原谅我迟到了。
words.en: To excuse someone means to forgive them for something they have done wrong or to allow them not to do something that they should do.

words.tr:
v. 急促而含混不清地说
n. 急促不清的话
words.ex: The children gabble when they are excited.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们兴奋时会叽叽喳喳地说个不停。
words.en: If you gabble, you say things so quickly that it is difficult for people to understand you.

words.ex: The gossip about the CEO made everyone shocked.
words.ex_cn: 关于CEO的流言蜚语让所有人都震惊了。
words.en: Gossip is informal conversation or reports about other people's private lives, which might be unkind or not true.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.tr: n. 传闻；谣传；道听途说
words.ex: He believed the hearsay without checking the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他没有核实事实就相信了这些流言。
words.en: Information received from other people that one cannot adequately substantiate; rumor.

words.ex: He spoke in a hoarse voice after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: If your voice is hoarse or if you are hoarse, your voice sounds rough and unclear, for example because your throat is sore.

words.ex: The hubbub in the market made it hard to think.
words.ex_cn: 市场里的喧闹让人难以集中思想。
words.en: A hubbub is a loud, confused noise, especially one caused by a large crowd of people.

words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.ex: He talked nonsense and no one understood him.
words.ex_cn: 他说了一些无意义的话，没人能理解他。
words.en: If you say that something spoken or written is nonsense, you mean that you consider it to be untrue or silly.

words.ex: He gave an oration at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了演讲。
words.en: A formal speech, especially one given on a ceremonial occasion.

words.ex: He outwit the opponent with a clever trick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个聪明的计策胜过了对手。
words.en: To outwit someone means to use your intelligence or a clever trick to defeat them or gain an advantage over them.

words.ex: He didn't refer to the book during the talk.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中没有提到那本书。
words.en: If you refer to a particular subject or person, you talk about them or mention them. If you refer to someone or something as a particular thing, you use a particular word, expression, or name to mention or describe them.

words.tr:
n. 隆隆声；辘辘声
v. 隆隆作响；辘辘行驶
words.ex: The dog let out a low rumble.
words.ex_cn: 狗发出了一声低沉的咆哮。
words.en: To make a continuous deep, resonant sound; to speak in a low, deep voice.

words.tr: v. 恳求；征求；（妓女）拉客
words.ex: He solicits donations for the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他为慈善机构募捐。
words.en: If you solicit money, help, support, or an opinion from someone, you ask them for it.

chapters.name: Word List 36 语言 说明

words.ex: She accentuates the first syllable when she says the word.
words.ex_cn: 她说这个词时重读第一个音节。
words.en: To accentuate something means to emphasize it or make it more noticeable.

words.tr:
n. 账户；叙述；账目；
v. 占…；说明；
words.ex: I opened a bank account last week.
words.ex_cn: 我上周开了一家银行账户。
words.en: An account is a detailed report or description of an event or situation.

words.ex: He cited a book in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他在文章中引用了一本书。
words.en: To cite something means to quote it or mention it as evidence or proof of what you are saying.

words.ex: Can you clarify your answer?
words.ex_cn: 你能澄清一下你的答案吗？
words.en: To clarify something means to make it easier to understand by explaining it more clearly.

words.tr: v. 解释；把…逐字译出；作句法分析
words.ex: He construes her silence as a yes.
words.ex_cn: 他把她的沉默理解为同意。
words.en: If you construe something in a particular way, you interpret it in that way.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.tr:
v. 包括；遮盖；报道；
n. 遮盖物；庇护所；封面；
words.ex: The book covers basic math and science.
words.ex_cn: 这本书包括基础数学和科学。
words.en: If something covers something else, it has been placed over or upon it, usually in order to protect it or hide it.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
